+  extend FriendlyId
+
+  validates :email, presence: true
+  validates :sender_id, presence: true
+  validates :team_id, presence: true
+  validate :limit_invitation_count
+
+  belongs_to :recipient, class_name: 'User'
+  belongs_to :sender, class_name: 'User'
+  belongs_to :team
+
+  delegate :name, to: :recipient, prefix: true, allow_nil: true
+
+  before_create :generate_code
+
+  friendly_id :code, use: [:finders]
+
+  def deliver
+    if save
+      InvitationMailer.delay.invitation(id)
+      true
+    else
+      false
+    end
+  end
+
+  def accept(user)
+    transaction do
+      update_attributes! accepted_at: Time.now, recipient: user
+      team.add_user(user)
+    end
+  end
+
+  def accepted?
+    accepted_at.present?
+  end
+
+  def has_users_remaining?
+    team.has_users_remaining?
+  end
+
+  def sender_name
+    sender.name
+  end
+
+  private
+
+  def generate_code
+    self.code = SecureRandom.hex(16)
+  end
+
+  def limit_invitation_count
+    if max_users_reached?
+      errors.add :team, 'has no users remaining'
+    end
+  end
+
+  def max_users_reached?
+    team.present? && !has_users_remaining?
+  end
+end

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.6  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.7  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.8  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.9  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.10  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.11  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.12  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.13  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.14  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.18  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.19  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Changes in circumstances
V.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
V.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART VI: Geographical limits
VI.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
VI.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART VII: Instalment agreements
VII.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
VII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART VIII: Currency
VIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
VIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART IX: Cancellation
IX.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
IX.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
IX.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART X: Notices
X.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
X.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XI: Accessibility
XI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XII: Complaints
XII.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XII.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XII.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XIII: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
XIII.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
XIII.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
XIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
XIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
XIII.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART XIV: Recovery of costs
XIV.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XV: Interest
XV.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVI: Waiver
XVI.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVII: How to read this document
XVII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XVII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XVII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XVIII: Flood
XVIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
XVIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XVIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XVIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XIX: Freezer contents
XIX.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
XIX.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART XX: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XX.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXI: Customer support
XXI.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXI.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART XXII: General exclusions
XXII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXII.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXII.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XXII.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
XXII.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
XXII.6  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART XXIII: Fraud
XXIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXIV: Governing law
XXIV.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXIV.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXV: Making a claim
XXV.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XXV.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXV.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

1. Definitions
1.1. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

1.10. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.11. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.12. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.13. Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.14. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.15. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.16. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

1.18. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.19. Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
1.20. Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
1.21. Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
1.22. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Trip Cancellation
3.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
3.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
4.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

5. Emergency Medical Expenses
5.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
5.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
5.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
5.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
5.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

6. Optional cover: Travel Delay
6.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
6.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

8. Making a claim
8.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

19. Discounts
19.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.

20. Notices
20.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.

22.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

23.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.

24.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
24.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

25. Records and evidence
25.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.

26.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.

27. Accessibility
27.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

28. Recovery of costs
28.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

29. Currency
29.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
29.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

30. Cancellation
30.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
30.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
30.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

31. Severability
31.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

32. Joint policyholders
32.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
32.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

33. Cooperation
33.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
33.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

34. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
34.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

35. Personal liability
35.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
35.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
35.3. The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

36. Arbitration
36.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
36.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

37. Interest
37.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

38. Subrogation
38.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
38.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

39. Emergency assistance
39.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
39.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
39.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

40. Market conditions
40.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

41. Sanctions
41.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

42. Payment of claims
42.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
42.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

43. Data protection
43.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
43.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
43.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

44.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
44.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

45.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
45.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

46. Assignment
46.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

47. Communication
47.1. We will communicate with you in English.
47.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

48. Complaints
48.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
48.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
48.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

49. Salvage
49.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
49.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

50.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.

51. Taxes
51.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.

52.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.

53.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.3** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.4** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
- **1.7** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.8** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.9** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
- **1.12** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.13** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.14** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.17** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.18** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Flood
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Escape of Water
- **6.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **6.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.6** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.3** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 9. Records and evidence
- **9.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **9.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **9.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 10. Notices
- **10.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **10.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 11. Geographical limits
- **11.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **11.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 12. Freezer contents
- **12.1** We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
- **12.2** We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

## 13. Premium payment
- **13.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **13.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 14. Tenant's improvements
- **14.1** If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
- **14.2** This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

## 15. Environmental commitment
- **15.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **15.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 16. Complaints
- **16.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **16.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **16.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 17. Waiver
- **17.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 18. Governing law
- **18.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **18.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 19. Subrogation
- **19.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **19.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 20. Garden and outdoor cover
- **20.1** We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
- **20.2** We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

## 21. Inflation
- **21.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **21.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 22. Currency
- **22.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **22.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 23. Joint policyholders
- **23.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **23.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 24. Interest
- **24.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 25. Reasonable precautions
- **25.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **25.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 26. Other insurance
- **26.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **26.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 27. Communication
- **27.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **27.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 28. Payment of claims
- **28.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **28.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 29. Discounts
- **29.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **29.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 30. Fraud
- **30.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **30.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 31. Compensation scheme
- **31.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **31.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 32. Renewal
- **32.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **32.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 33. Taxes
- **33.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **33.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 34. Assignment
- **34.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 35. Cancellation
- **35.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **35.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **35.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 36. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **36.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 37. Market conditions
- **37.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 38. Exchange of information
- **38.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **38.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 39. Automatic renewal
- **39.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **39.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 40. Data protection
- **40.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **40.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **40.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 41. Customer support
- **41.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **41.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 42. Sanctions
- **42.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 43. Third-party administrators
- **43.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **43.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 44. Contents temporarily removed
- **44.1** Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
- **44.2** Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

## 45. Salvage
- **45.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **45.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 46. Electronic documents
- **46.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **46.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **46.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 47. Changes in circumstances
- **47.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **47.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 48. Instalment agreements
- **48.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **48.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 49. Alternative accommodation
- **49.1** If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
- **49.2** We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
- **49.3** Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

## 50. Locks and keys
- **50.1** If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
- **50.2** The most we will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

## 51. Accessibility
- **51.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 52. Change of address
- **52.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **52.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 53. Cooperation
- **53.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **53.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 54. Severability
- **54.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 55. Recovery of costs
- **55.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 56. Duty of fair presentation
- **56.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **56.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **56.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 57. Interpretation
- **57.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **57.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **57.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 58. Arbitration
- **58.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **58.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

From: Tomas Gallagher

Hello,

I would like to claim under Escape of Water for an antique rug. My policy started on January 30, 2025 and my schedule lists Theft, Escape of Water, Flood (extensions: none). The incident happened on May 28, 2025. A pipe under the kitchen sink burst suddenly during a cold night and soaked the antique rug. Tomas works from home three days a week. A neighbour reported the incident to the building manager.

I am sending this on August 19, 2025, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $1,964.

Thanks,
Tomas

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Group Health Cash Plan
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.2** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.3** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.4** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.5** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.6** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Inflation
- **3.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **3.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. Geographical limits
- **5.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **5.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 6. Leaving the plan
- **6.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **6.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 7. Customer support
- **7.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **7.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 8. Renewal
- **8.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **8.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 9. Appeals
- **9.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **9.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **9.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 10. Payment of claims
- **10.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **10.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 11. Complaints
- **11.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **11.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **11.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 12. Environmental commitment
- **12.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **12.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 13. Eligibility
- **13.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **13.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 14. Interpretation
- **14.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **14.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **14.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 15. Wellness allowance
- **15.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **15.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 16. Compensation scheme
- **16.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **16.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 17. Dependants
- **17.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **17.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 18. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **18.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **18.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **18.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **18.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 19. General exclusions
- **19.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **19.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **19.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 20. Electronic documents
- **20.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **20.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **20.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 21. Coordination of benefits
- **21.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **21.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 22. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **22.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 23. Recovery of costs
- **23.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 24. Cancellation
- **24.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **24.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **24.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 25. Making a claim
- **25.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **25.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **25.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 26. Subrogation
- **26.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **26.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 27. Exchange of information
- **27.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **27.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 28. Market conditions
- **28.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 29. Change of address
- **29.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **29.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 30. Communication
- **30.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **30.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 31. Fraud
- **31.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **31.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 32. Taxes
- **32.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **32.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Issued by Brightline Device Cover

I.12  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.

I.14  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.15  Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
I.16  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Customer's details, the covers the Customer bought and any extensions.
I.17  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.18  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Data and backups
III.1  The Provider is not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on the Customer's device.
III.2  The Customer should back up the Customer's data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

PART IV: Claims documents
IV.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
IV.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART V: Discounts
V.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
V.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART VI: Customer support
VI.1  The Provider's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
VI.2  Outside these hours the Customer can leave a message and the Provider will call back on the next working day.

PART VII: Change of address
VII.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
VII.2  The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART VIII: Third-party administrators
VIII.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
VIII.2  Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART IX: Currency
IX.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
IX.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART X: Sanctions
X.1  The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XI: Records and evidence
XI.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.

PART XII: Market conditions

PART XIII: Transferring the plan

PART XIV: Interpretation
XIV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XIV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XIV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XIX: Communication

TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(b) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
(c) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(d) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(e) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
(g) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(h) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 7. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 8. Personal liability
(a) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(b) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

Article 9. Records and evidence
(a) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 10. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 11. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 12. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 13. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

Article 14. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 15. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 16. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 17. Assignment
(a) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 18. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 19. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 20. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 21. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 22. Missed departure
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 10. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

Article 12. Changes in circumstances

Article 13. Cooperation

(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 14. Change of address

(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 15. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 16. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 17. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.

Article 21. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 22. Records and evidence
(a) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 23. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 24. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 25. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Benefits Trust

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.2 Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.3 Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.4 Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.5 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.6 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.7 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.8 Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.9 Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.10 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.11 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.12 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.13 Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - VISION CARE
3.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
3.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
3.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
3.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 4 - DENTAL CARE
4.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
4.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
4.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
4.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 5 - THERAPY SERVICES
5.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
5.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
5.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
5.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 6 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
6.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
6.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
6.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - FRAUD
9.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
9.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 10 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
10.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
10.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 11 - ACCESSIBILITY
11.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 12 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
12.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
12.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 13 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
13.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
13.2 If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 14 - COMPLAINTS
14.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
14.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
14.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 15 - DISCOUNTS
15.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.

SECTION 16 - ASSIGNMENT
16.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 17 - DATA PROTECTION
17.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
17.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
17.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

18.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

SECTION 19 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
19.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
19.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 20 - CURRENCY
20.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.

SECTION 21 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
21.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.

21.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

22.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

23.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.

SECTION 24 - SANCTIONS
24.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 25 - NOTICES
25.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
25.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 26 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
26.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
26.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
26.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 27 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
27.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
27.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 28 - GOVERNING LAW
28.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
28.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 29 - SALVAGE
29.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
29.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 30 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
30.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
30.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 31 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
31.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 32 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
32.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 33 - MARKET CONDITIONS
33.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 34 - COORDINATION OF BENEFITS
34.1 If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
34.2 You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

SECTION 35 - ARBITRATION
35.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
35.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 36 - INFLATION
36.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
36.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 37 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
37.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
37.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 38 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
38.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
38.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
38.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 39 - COMMUNICATION
39.1 We will communicate with you in English.
39.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 40 - TAXES
40.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
40.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 41 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
41.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
41.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
41.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 42 - SUBROGATION
42.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
42.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 43 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
43.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
43.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 44 - DEPENDANTS
44.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
44.2 Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

SECTION 45 - RENEWAL
45.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
45.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 46 - INTERPRETATION
46.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
46.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
46.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 47 - OTHER INSURANCE
47.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
47.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 48 - WELLNESS ALLOWANCE
48.1 Each plan year you may claim up to $150 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
48.2 The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SECTION 49 - LEAVING THE PLAN
49.1 Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
49.2 Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

SECTION 50 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
50.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
50.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 51 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
51.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
51.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 52 - INTEREST
52.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 53 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS

54.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.

SECTION 55 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
55.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
55.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 56 - ELIGIBILITY
56.1 Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.

57.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.
