SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.2 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.3 Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.4 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.6 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.8 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.9 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.10 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.11 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.12 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.13 Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.14 Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
1.15 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.16 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.17 Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.18 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.19 Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
1.20 Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
1.21 Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
1.22 Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: TRAVEL DELAY
3.1 We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

SECTION 4 - TRIP CANCELLATION
4.1 We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
4.5 We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

SECTION 5 - BAGGAGE AND PERSONAL BELONGINGS
5.1 We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
5.2 The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
5.3 The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
5.5 We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
5.6 We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

SECTION 6 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
6.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
6.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
6.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
6.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
6.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
6.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.3 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.3 You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 9 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
9.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
9.2 If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 10 - MISSED DEPARTURE
10.1 We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
10.2 You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

SECTION 11 - SEVERABILITY
11.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 12 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
12.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
12.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 13 - MARKET CONDITIONS
13.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 14 - SUBROGATION
14.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
14.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 15 - REPATRIATION
15.1 If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
15.2 We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

SECTION 16 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
16.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
16.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 17 - LEGAL EXPENSES ABROAD
17.1 We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
17.2 We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

SECTION 18 - DATA PROTECTION
18.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
18.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
18.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 19 - DISCOUNTS
19.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
19.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 20 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
20.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 21 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
21.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
21.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 22 - CURRENCY
22.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
22.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 23 - OTHER INSURANCE
23.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
23.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 24 - ARBITRATION
24.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
24.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 25 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
25.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
25.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 26 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
26.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
26.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 27 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
27.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
27.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 28 - RENTAL CAR EXCESS
28.1 If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
28.2 This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

SECTION 29 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
29.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 30 - SALVAGE
30.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
30.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 31 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
31.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
31.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 32 - FRAUD
32.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
32.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 33 - ASSIGNMENT
33.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 34 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
34.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
34.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 35 - SANCTIONS
35.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 36 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
36.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
36.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
36.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 37 - CANCELLATION
37.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
37.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
37.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 38 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
38.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
38.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 39 - INFLATION
39.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
39.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 40 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
40.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
40.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 41 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
41.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
41.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 42 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
42.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
42.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 43 - COOPERATION
43.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
43.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 44 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
44.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
44.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
44.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 45 - NOTICES
45.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
45.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 46 - GOVERNING LAW
46.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
46.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 47 - COMPLAINTS
47.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
47.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
47.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 48 - TAXES
48.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
48.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 49 - COMMUNICATION
49.1 We will communicate with you in English.
49.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 50 - EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE
50.1 Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
50.2 You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
50.3 The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

SECTION 51 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
51.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
51.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
51.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

52.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
52.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
52.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

III.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART IV: Optional cover: Travel Delay
IV.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART V: Baggage and Personal Belongings
V.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
V.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART VI: Emergency Medical Expenses
VI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
VI.5  The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
VI.6  The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.2  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART IX: Changes in circumstances
IX.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
IX.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART X: Salvage
X.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
X.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XI: Claims documents
XI.1  The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XI.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XII: Currency
XII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XIII: Assignment
XIII.1  The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

PART XIV: Market conditions
XIV.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XV: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XV.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XVI: Reasonable precautions
XVI.1  The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XVI.2  The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XVII: Notices
XVII.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
XVII.2  Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XVIII: Personal liability
XVIII.1  The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
XVIII.2  This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
XVIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

PART XIX: Arbitration
XIX.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XIX.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

PART XX: Taxes
XX.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XX.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXI: Governing law
XXI.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXI.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXII: Instalment agreements
XXII.1  If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXIII: Records and evidence
XXIII.1  The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXIII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXIII.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXIV: Communication
XXIV.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
XXIV.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXV: Inflation
XXV.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXV.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXVI: Recovery of costs
XXVI.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

PART XXVII: Automatic renewal
XXVII.1  Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XXVII.2  The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XXVIII: Premium payment
XXVIII.1  The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXVIII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXIX: Other insurance
XXIX.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XXIX.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

PART XXX: Missed departure
XXX.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
XXX.2  The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

PART XXXI: Cooperation
XXXI.1  The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXXI.2  The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART XXXII: Discounts
XXXII.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXXII.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XXXIII: Environmental commitment
XXXIII.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXXIII.2  The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXXIV: Electronic documents
XXXIV.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
XXXIV.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
XXXIV.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXXV: How to read this document
XXXV.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XXXV.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XXXV.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XXXVI: Interest
XXXVI.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXXVII: Legal expenses abroad
XXXVII.1  The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
XXXVII.2  The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

PART XXXVIII: Data protection
XXXVIII.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXXVIII.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXXVIII.3  The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7. Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.9. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.10. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.11. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.12. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.13. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.14. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.15. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.19. Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.20. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.21. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.

3.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

4.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

5.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.

5.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

6.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
6.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
6.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

7. Vision Care

7.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
7.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

8. Sanctions
8.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

9. Salvage
9.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
9.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

10. Data protection
10.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
10.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
10.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

11. Therapy Services
11.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
11.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
11.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
11.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

12. Other insurance
12.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
12.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

13. Coordination of benefits

14.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

15. Assignment

16. Renewal
16.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
16.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

17. Changes in circumstances
17.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
17.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

19.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
19.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
19.4. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
19.5. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
19.6. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

21.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

22.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

23. Payment of claims
23.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
23.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

24. Waiver
24.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

25. Premium payment
25.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.

PART I: Definitions

I.9  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.10  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.11  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.12  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.13  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.14  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.15  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.16  Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Vision Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
III.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
III.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART IV: Therapy Services
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART V: Optional cover: Hearing Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
V.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART VI: Dental Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
VI.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
VI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
VI.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
VI.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
VI.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.4  The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.2  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART IX: Communication
IX.1  The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
IX.2  The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART X: Payment of claims
X.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
X.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XI: Third-party administrators
XI.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
XI.2  Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XII: Eligibility
XII.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
XII.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

PART XIII: Environmental commitment
XIII.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XIII.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XIV: Automatic renewal
XIV.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XIV.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XV: Instalment agreements
XV.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XV.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XVI: Fraud
XVI.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XVI.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XVII: Reasonable precautions
XVII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XVII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XVIII: Duty of fair presentation
XVIII.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XVIII.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XVIII.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XIX: Exchange of information
XIX.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XIX.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART XX: Recovery of costs
XX.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXI: Wellness allowance
XXI.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXI.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXII: Cooperation
XXII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XXIII: Customer support
XXIII.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXIII.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART XXIV: Complaints
XXIV.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXIV.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXIV.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXV: Accessibility
XXV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXVI: Dependants
XXVI.1  The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
XXVI.2  Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

PART XXVII: Change of address
XXVII.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXVII.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXVIII: Compensation scheme
XXVIII.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXVIII.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXIX: Interest
XXIX.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXX: Assignment
XXX.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XXXI: Salvage
XXXI.1  When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
XXXI.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

PART XXXII: Claims documents
XXXII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXXII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIII: Premium payment
XXXIII.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXXIII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXXIV: Subrogation
XXXIV.1  The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXXIV.2  The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXXV: Inflation
XXXV.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXV.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Renters Contents Protection
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.3** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.4** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Alternative accommodation
- **3.1** If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
- **3.2** We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
- **3.3** Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

## 4. Salvage
- **4.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **4.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Claims documents
- **6.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **6.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 7. Flood
- **7.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **7.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
- **7.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **7.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 8. Cancellation
- **8.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **8.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
- **8.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 9. Arbitration
- **9.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **9.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 10. Escape of Water
- **10.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **10.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
- **10.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **10.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 11. Instalment agreements
- **11.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **11.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 12. Geographical limits
- **12.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **12.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 13. Premium payment
- **13.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **13.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 14. Other insurance
- **14.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **14.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 15. General exclusions
- **15.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **15.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **15.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 16. Exchange of information
- **16.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **16.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 17. Severability
- **17.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 18. Reasonable precautions
- **18.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **18.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 19. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **19.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 20. Market conditions
- **20.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 21. Environmental commitment
- **21.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **21.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 22. Third-party administrators
- **22.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **22.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 23. Customer support
- **23.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **23.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 24. Changes in circumstances
- **24.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **24.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 25. Communication
- **25.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **25.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 26. Recovery of costs
- **26.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 27. Renewal
- **27.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **27.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 28. Interest
- **28.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 29. Making a claim
- **29.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **29.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **29.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 30. Cooperation
- **30.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **30.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 31. Data protection
- **31.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **31.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **31.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
I.2  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.3  Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
I.4  Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
I.5  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.6  Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
I.7  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.8  Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
I.9  Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.10  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
I.11  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
I.12  Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
I.13  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.14  Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Baggage and Personal Belongings
III.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.

Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.

I.3  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.4  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Flood
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VIII: Taxes
VIII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
VIII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART IX: Discounts
IX.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
IX.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART X: Currency
X.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
X.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XI: Exchange of information
XI.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
XI.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

PART XII: Cancellation
XII.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XII.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
XII.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XIII: Data protection
XIII.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIII.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIII.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XIV: Complaints
XIV.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XIV.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XIV.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XV: Duty of fair presentation
XV.1  The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
XV.2  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XV.3  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XVI: Reasonable precautions
XVI.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XVI.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XVII: Market conditions
XVII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XVIII: Claims documents
XVIII.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XVIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XIX: Contents temporarily removed
XIX.1  The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
XIX.2  Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

PART XX: Alternative accommodation
XX.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
XX.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
XX.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART XXI: Payment of claims
XXI.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XXI.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XXII: Interpretation
XXII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXII.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXII.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXIII: Communication
XXIII.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXIV: Subrogation
XXIV.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXIV.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXV: Salvage
XXV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XXV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.
