CASE PRESENTATION A
TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.2 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.3 Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.4 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
1.6 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.8 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.9 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
1.10 Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
1.11 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.12 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.13 Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.14 Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
1.15 Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - BAGGAGE AND PERSONAL BELONGINGS
3.1 We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
3.5 We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
3.6 We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

SECTION 4 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
4.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
4.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
4.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
4.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
4.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 5 - OPTIONAL COVER: TRAVEL DELAY
5.1 We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
5.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3 We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

SECTION 6 - TRIP CANCELLATION
6.1 We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
6.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
6.3 The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
6.4 We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
6.5 We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.3 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.4 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 9 - EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE
9.1 Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
9.2 You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
9.3 The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

SECTION 10 - COOPERATION
10.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
10.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 11 - RENEWAL
11.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
11.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 12 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
12.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
12.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 13 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
13.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
13.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 14 - CANCELLATION
14.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
14.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
14.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 15 - ASSIGNMENT
15.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 16 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
16.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
16.2 If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 17 - INTERPRETATION
17.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
17.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
17.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 18 - SUBROGATION
18.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
18.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 19 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
19.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
19.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 20 - SALVAGE
20.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
20.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 21 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
21.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
21.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
21.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 22 - ARBITRATION
22.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
22.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 23 - COMPLAINTS
23.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
23.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
23.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 24 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
24.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
24.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
24.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 25 - DISCOUNTS
25.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
25.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 26 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
26.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
26.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 27 - INTEREST
27.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 28 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
28.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
28.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 29 - CURRENCY
29.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
29.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 30 - TAXES
30.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
30.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 31 - WAIVER
31.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 32 - SANCTIONS
32.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 33 - GOVERNING LAW
33.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
33.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 34 - SEVERABILITY
34.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 35 - ACCESSIBILITY
35.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 36 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
36.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 37 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
37.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
37.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 38 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
38.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 39 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
39.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
39.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 40 - RENTAL CAR EXCESS
40.1 If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
40.2 This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

SECTION 41 - DATA PROTECTION
41.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
41.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
41.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 42 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
42.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
42.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 43 - REPATRIATION
43.1 If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
43.2 We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

SECTION 44 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
44.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
44.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 45 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
45.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
45.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 46 - PERSONAL LIABILITY
46.1 We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
46.2 This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
46.3 The most we will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

SECTION 47 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
47.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
47.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 48 - MISSED DEPARTURE
48.1 We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
48.2 You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

SECTION 49 - NOTICES
49.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
49.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 50 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
50.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
50.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 51 - FRAUD
51.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
51.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 52 - MARKET CONDITIONS
52.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 53 - LEGAL EXPENSES ABROAD
53.1 We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
53.2 We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

SECTION 54 - COMMUNICATION
54.1 We will communicate with you in English.
54.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 55 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
55.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
55.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
55.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 56 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
56.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
56.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 57 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
57.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
57.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 58 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
58.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
58.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
58.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 59 - OTHER INSURANCE
59.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
59.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 60 - INFLATION
60.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
60.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

# Renters Contents Protection
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.3** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.4** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.5** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.6** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.7** Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
- **1.8** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.9** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.10** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.11** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.12** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.13** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
- **1.14** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.15** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.16** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.17** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.18** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.19** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.20** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.21** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Flood
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Escape of Water
- **6.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **6.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **7.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

I.4  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.5  Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
I.6  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.7  Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
I.8  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.9  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
I.10  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
I.11  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.12  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.13  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
II.4  The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Sanctions
III.1  The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART IV: Unrecoverable devices
IV.1  If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
IV.2  The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

PART V: Interpretation
V.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
V.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
V.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART VI: Third-party administrators
VI.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
VI.2  Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART VII: Communication
VII.1  The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
VII.2  The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART VIII: How to read this document
VIII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
VIII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
VIII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART IX: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
IX.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
IX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
IX.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IX.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
IX.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART X: Records and evidence
X.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
X.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
X.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XI: Accidental Damage
XI.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
XI.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
XI.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
XI.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
XI.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART XII: Change of address
XII.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
XII.2  The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XIII: Breakdown
XIII.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
XIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XIII.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
XIII.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
XIII.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART XIV: Changes in circumstances
XIV.1  The Customer must tell the Provider as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XIV.2  The Provider may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XV: Compensation scheme
XV.1  The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XV.2  If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XVI: General exclusions
XVI.1  The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XVI.2  The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XVI.3  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
XVI.4  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

PART XVII: Making a claim
XVII.1  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

XVII.3  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART XVIII: Claims documents
XVIII.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
XVIII.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XIX: Data protection
XIX.1  The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIX.2  The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIX.3  The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

PART XX: Premium payment
XX.1  The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXI: Cancellation
XXI.1  The Customer can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XXI.2  After the first 14 days the Customer can cancel at any time; the Provider will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
XXI.3  The Provider can cancel this policy by giving the Customer 30 days' written notice to the last address the Provider holds.

PART XXII: Environmental commitment
XXII.1  Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXII.2  The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXIII: Replacement devices
XXIII.1  If the Provider cannot repair the Customer's device economically, the Provider will replace it with a replacement device.
XXIII.2  Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.

Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.

1.4. Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.5. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.6. Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.7. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.8. High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.9. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.10. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.11. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.12. Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Premium payment
3.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
3.2. If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

4. Freezer contents
4.1. We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
4.2. We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

5. Compensation scheme
5.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
5.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

6. Complaints
6.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
6.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
6.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

7. Alternative accommodation
7.1. If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
7.2. We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
7.3. Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

8. Discounts
8.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
8.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

9. Theft
9.1. We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
9.2. The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
9.3. The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
9.4. We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
9.5. We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
9.6. We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

10. Notices
10.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
10.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

11. Currency
11.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
11.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

12. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
12.1. We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
12.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
12.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
12.4. We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
12.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

13. Environmental commitment
13.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
13.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

14. Changes in circumstances
14.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
14.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

15. Electronic documents
15.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
15.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
15.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

16. Flood
16.1. We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
16.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
16.3. The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
16.4. We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

17. Governing law
17.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
17.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

18. Escape of Water
18.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
18.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
18.3. We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
18.4. We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

19. Interest
19.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

20. Communication
20.1. We will communicate with you in English.
20.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

21. Third-party administrators
21.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
21.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

22. Records and evidence
22.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
22.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
22.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

23. Exchange of information
23.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
23.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

24. Joint policyholders
24.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
24.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

25. Market conditions
25.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

26. Interpretation
26.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
26.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
26.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

27. How to read this document
27.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
27.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
27.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

28. General exclusions
28.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
28.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
28.3. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
28.4. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
28.5. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

29. Contents temporarily removed
29.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
29.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

30. Waiver
30.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

31. Fraud
31.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
31.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

32. Arbitration
32.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
32.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

33. Garden and outdoor cover
33.1. We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
33.2. We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

34. Making a claim
34.1. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
34.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
34.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

35. Reasonable precautions
35.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
35.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

state.policy:
GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services
In this policy, "the Plan" means Cedar Benefits Services and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(b) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(c) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(d) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(e) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 4. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 6. Making a claim
(a) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 7. Appeals
(a) If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
(b) An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
(c) The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

Article 8. Coordination of benefits
(a) If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
(b) The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

Article 9. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 10. Dependants
(a) The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
(b) Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

Article 11. Notices
(a) Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
(b) Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 12. Compensation scheme
(a) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 13. Complaints
(a) If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 14. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
(b) The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

Article 15. Assignment
(a) The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

Article 16. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 17. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 18. Records and evidence
(a) The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 19. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 20. Arbitration
(a) If the Plan accepts a claim but disagree with the Member about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

Article 21. Premium payment
(a) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 22. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 23. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

Article 24. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 25. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 26. Change of address
(a) The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
(b) The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 27. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 28. Eligibility
(a) Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
(b) Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

Article 29. Interest
(a) The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 30. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

Article 31. Communication
(a) The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
(b) The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 32. Payment of claims
(a) The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
(b) The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

Article 33. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

1.17 Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.18 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

2.1 Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 4 - VISION CARE
4.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.

SECTION 5 - THERAPY SERVICES
5.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.

SECTION 13 - MARKET CONDITIONS
13.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

18.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
18.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 19 - CURRENCY
19.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
19.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 20 - ARBITRATION
20.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
20.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 21 - COOPERATION
21.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
21.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 22 - DEPENDANTS
22.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.

SECTION 23 - ACCESSIBILITY

24.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.

25.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.

Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.

- **1.3** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.

- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

- **3.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **3.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

- **4.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

- **5.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **5.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 6. Communication

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7. Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.9. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.10. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.11. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.12. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.13. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.14. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.15. Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.16. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.17. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Arbitration
3.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
3.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

4. Complaints
4.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
4.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
4.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

5. Market conditions
5.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

6. Environmental commitment
6.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
6.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

7. Cooperation
7.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
7.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

8. Instalment agreements
8.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
8.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

9. Coordination of benefits
9.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
9.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

10. Change of address
10.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
10.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

11. Dental Care
11.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
11.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
11.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
11.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
11.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
11.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

12. Appeals
12.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
12.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
12.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

13. Waiver
13.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

14. Notices
14.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
14.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

15. Wellness allowance
15.1. Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
15.2. The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

16. Changes in circumstances
16.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
16.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

17. Exchange of information
17.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
17.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

18. Leaving the plan
18.1. Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
18.2. Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

19. Compensation scheme
19.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
19.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

20. Severability
20.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

21. Currency
21.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
21.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

22. Cancellation
22.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
22.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
22.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

23. Subrogation
23.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
23.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

24. Accessibility
24.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

25. Interest
25.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

26. Claims documents
26.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
26.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

27. Geographical limits
27.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
27.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

28. Taxes
28.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
28.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

29. How to read this document
29.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
29.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
29.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

36.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.

39.1 We will communicate with you in English.

40.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
40.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

41.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.

42.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 43 - RENEWAL
43.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.

46.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.

47.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

48.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.

49.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 50 - WAIVER
50.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

51.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
51.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.

53.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Baggage and Personal Belongings
III.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
IV.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
V.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
V.3  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VI: Personal liability
VI.1  The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
VI.2  This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

PART VII: Customer support
VII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
VII.2  Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART VIII: Change of address
VIII.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
VIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART IX: Renewal
IX.1  The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
IX.2  The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART X: Taxes
X.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
X.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XI: Exchange of information
XI.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
XI.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

PART XII: Other insurance
XII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XII.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

PART XIII: Fraud
XIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XIV: Salvage
XIV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XIV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XV: Cancellation
XV.1  The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XV.2  After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XV.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XVI: Missed departure
XVI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
XVI.2  The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

PART XVII: Automatic renewal
XVII.1  Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XVII.2  The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XVIII: Rental car excess
XVIII.1  If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
XVIII.2  This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

PART XIX: Data protection
XIX.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIX.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIX.3  The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XX: Arbitration
XX.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XX.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

PART XXI: Accessibility
XXI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXII: Discounts
XXII.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXII.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XXIII: Environmental commitment
XXIII.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXIII.2  The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXIV: Reasonable precautions
XXIV.1  The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXIV.2  The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXV: Sanctions
XXV.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXVI: Severability
XXVI.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

1.12. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
