CASE PRESENTATION B
GADGET COVER: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Issued by Circuit Care Services

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2 Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3 Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.4 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.5 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.6 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7 Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
1.8 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.9 Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.10 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.11 Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND SERVICE FEE
2.1 Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.2 Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
2.3 Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.4 The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
3.1 We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
3.2 The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
3.5 We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

SECTION 4 - BREAKDOWN
4.1 We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
4.5 We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

SECTION 5 - OPTIONAL COVER: THEFT AND LOSS
5.1 We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
5.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3 The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
5.5 We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

SECTION 6 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
6.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
6.3 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
6.4 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
6.5 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.6 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

SECTION 7 - MAKING A CLAIM
7.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
7.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
7.3 You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 8 - OTHER INSURANCE
8.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
8.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 9 - REPLACEMENT DEVICES
9.1 If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
9.2 Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
9.3 Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

SECTION 10 - COMMUNICATION
10.1 We will communicate with you in English.
10.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 11 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
11.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
11.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 12 - TAXES
12.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
12.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 13 - WAIVER
13.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 14 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
14.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
14.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
14.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 15 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
15.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
15.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 16 - NOTICES
16.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
16.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 17 - SOFTWARE SUPPORT
17.1 Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
17.2 Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

SECTION 18 - COOPERATION
18.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
18.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 19 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
19.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
19.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 20 - REPAIR PROCESS
20.1 After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
20.2 We aim to return repaired devices within 5 business days of receiving them.

SECTION 21 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
21.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
21.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 22 - FRAUD
22.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
22.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 23 - ASSIGNMENT
23.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 24 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
24.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
24.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
24.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 25 - INFLATION
25.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
25.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 26 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
26.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 27 - ACCESSIBILITY
27.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 28 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
28.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
28.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 29 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
29.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
29.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 30 - SALVAGE
30.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
30.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 31 - ARBITRATION
31.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
31.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 32 - RENEWAL
32.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
32.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 33 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
33.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
33.2 If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(b) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(c) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(d) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(e) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(f) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(g) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(h) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
(i) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(j) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
(k) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(l) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(m) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(n) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 6. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 9. Cooperation
(a) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 10. Premium payment
(a) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 11. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 12. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
(b) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 13. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 14. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

Article 15. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 16. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 17. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 18. Personal liability
(a) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(b) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

Article 19. Missed departure
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

Article 20. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 21. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 22. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 23. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 24. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 25. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 26. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 27. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 28. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

Article 29. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 30. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

Article 31. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 32. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 33. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 34. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 35. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 36. Records and evidence
(a) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 37. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 38. Governing law

(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 39. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 41. How to read this document

(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.

I.4  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Instalment agreements
III.1  If the Customer pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
III.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART IV: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
IV.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
IV.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IV.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
IV.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART V: Discounts
V.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
V.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART VI: Transferring the plan
VI.1  The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
VI.2  The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

PART VII: Repair process
VII.1  After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
VII.2  The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 15 business days of receiving them.

PART VIII: Records and evidence
VIII.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
VIII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
VIII.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART IX: Breakdown
IX.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
IX.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
IX.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
IX.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
IX.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART X: General exclusions
X.1  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
X.2  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.

PART XI: Complaints
XI.1  If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XI.2  The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XI.3  If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XII: Making a claim
XII.1  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XII.2  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XII.3  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART XIII: How to read this document
XIII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XIII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XIII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XIV: Renewal
XIV.1  The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XIV.2  The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XV: Severability

3.2 The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.

3.5 We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.

5.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

6.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
6.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

7.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.3 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.4 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

state.policy:
STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.3  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.4  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.5  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.6  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.7  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.8  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.9  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.10  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.11  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.12  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.13  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.14  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.15  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.16  Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Vision Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
III.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
III.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART IV: Therapy Services
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART V: Optional cover: Hearing Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
V.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART VI: Dental Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
VI.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
VI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
VI.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
VI.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
VI.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.4  The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.2  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART IX: Communication
IX.1  The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
IX.2  The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART X: Payment of claims
X.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
X.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XI: Third-party administrators
XI.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
XI.2  Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XII: Eligibility
XII.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
XII.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

PART XIII: Environmental commitment
XIII.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XIII.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XIV: Automatic renewal
XIV.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XIV.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XV: Instalment agreements
XV.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XV.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XVI: Fraud
XVI.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XVI.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XVII: Reasonable precautions
XVII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XVII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XVIII: Duty of fair presentation
XVIII.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XVIII.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XVIII.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XIX: Exchange of information
XIX.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XIX.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART XX: Recovery of costs
XX.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXI: Wellness allowance
XXI.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXI.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXII: Cooperation
XXII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XXIII: Customer support
XXIII.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXIII.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART XXIV: Complaints
XXIV.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXIV.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXIV.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXV: Accessibility
XXV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXVI: Dependants
XXVI.1  The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
XXVI.2  Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

PART XXVII: Change of address
XXVII.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXVII.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXVIII: Compensation scheme
XXVIII.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXVIII.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXIX: Interest
XXIX.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXX: Assignment
XXX.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XXXI: Salvage
XXXI.1  When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
XXXI.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

PART XXXII: Claims documents
XXXII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXXII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIII: Premium payment
XXXIII.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXXIII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXXIV: Subrogation
XXXIV.1  The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXXIV.2  The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXXV: Inflation
XXXV.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXV.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

state.policy:
HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(f) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(g) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(h) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(i) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(j) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(k) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(l) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(m) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(n) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(o) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(p) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 4. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 5. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 6. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 7. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 8. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 9. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 10. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 11. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 12. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 13. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 14. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 15. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 16. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 17. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 18. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 19. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 20. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 21. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 22. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 23. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 24. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 25. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 26. Locks and keys
(a) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

Article 27. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 28. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 29. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 30. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 31. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 32. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 33. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 34. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 35. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 36. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 37. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 38. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 39. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 40. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.4  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.5  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.6  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.7  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.2  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.3  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.4  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.5  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.6  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.7  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.8  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Dental Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
III.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
III.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
III.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART IV: Optional cover: Hearing Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
IV.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART V: Therapy Services
V.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
VI.2  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.2  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART VIII: Coordination of benefits
VIII.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
VIII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.6** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.7** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.10** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.11** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.12** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.13** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.14** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.15** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.16** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.17** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.18** Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.19** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.20** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Vision Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **3.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **3.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **5.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **5.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 6. Therapy Services
- **6.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **6.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **6.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.4** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.5** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.

I.7  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.8  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.9  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.10  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.11  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.12  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.13  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.14  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.15  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.

V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

18.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.

19.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.

20. Discounts
20.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.

21.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.

25.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
25.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.

27. Sanctions
27.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

28. Accessibility
28.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

29. Governing law

30. Taxes
30.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.

+#!/usr/bin/env python
 
+from __future__ import print_function
+
+import unittest
+
+try:
+    from unittest import mock
+except ImportError:
+    import mock
+
+import imp
+import os.path
+
+
+import engines
+
+
+class TestInit(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_init(self):
+        mock_engines = {}
+
+        mock_listdir = mock.Mock(return_value=(
+                'text_engine.txt',
+                '0_engine.py',
+                '.period_engine.py',
+                '@at_engine.py',
+                '__init__.py',
+                '_underscore_engine.py',
+                'normal_engine.py',
+                'compiled_engine.pyc',
+                'optimized_engine.pyo',
+            ))
+
+        valid_engines = {
+                '_underscore_engine':   ('UnderscoreEngine', 'underscore'),
+                'normal_engine':        ('NormalEngine',     'normal'),
+                'compiled_engine':      ('CompiledEngine',   'compiled'),
+                'optimized_engine':     ('OptimizedEngine',  'optimized'),
+            }
+
+        result_dict = {handle: None for __, (__, handle) in valid_engines.items()}
+
+        def mock_import_module(name, package):
+            self.assertEqual(package, 'engines')
+
+            assert name.startswith('.')
+            name = name[1:]
+
+            module = imp.new_module('%s.%s' % (package, name))
+
+            if name == '__init__':
+                module.Engine = engines.Engine
+            else:
+                self.assertIn(name, valid_engines)
+                class_name, engine_handle = valid_engines[name]
+
+                class MockEngine(engines.Engine):
+                    handle = engine_handle
+
+                MockEngine.__name__ = class_name
+                MockEngine.__qualname__ = class_name
+
+                result_dict[engine_handle] = MockEngine
+                setattr(module, class_name, MockEngine)
+
+            return module
+
+        with mock.patch.object(engines, 'engines', mock_engines), \
+             mock.patch('os.listdir', mock_listdir), \
+             mock.patch('importlib.import_module', mock_import_module):
+            engines._init()
+
+        mock_listdir.assert_called_once_with(os.path.dirname(engines.__file__))
+        self.assertDictEqual(mock_engines, result_dict)
+
+
+class TestEngine(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_not_instantiable(self):
+        self.assertRaises(AssertionError, engines.Engine, dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+    def test_handle_is_none(self):
+        class TestEngine(engines.Engine):
+            pass
+
+        engine = TestEngine(dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+        self.assertIsNone(engine.handle)
+
+    def test_apply_not_implemented(self):
+        class TestEngine(engines.Engine):
+            pass
+
+        engine = TestEngine(dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+        self.assertRaises(NotImplementedError, engine.apply, {})
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()
+

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7. Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.9. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.10. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.11. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.12. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.13. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.14. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.15. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.19. Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.20. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.21. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Governing law
3.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
3.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

4. Claims documents
4.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
4.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

5. Optional cover: Hearing Care
5.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
5.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

6. Appeals
6.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
6.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
6.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

7. Vision Care
7.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
7.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
7.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
7.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

8. Sanctions
8.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

9. Salvage
9.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
9.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

10. Data protection
10.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
10.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
10.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

11. Therapy Services
11.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
11.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
11.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
11.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

12. Other insurance
12.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
12.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

13. Coordination of benefits
13.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
13.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

14. Environmental commitment
14.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
14.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

15. Assignment
15.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

16. Renewal
16.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
16.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

17. Changes in circumstances
17.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
17.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

18. Dental Care
18.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
18.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
18.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
18.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
18.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
18.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

19. General exclusions
19.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
19.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
19.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
19.4. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
19.5. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
19.6. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

20. Customer support
20.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
20.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

21. Making a claim
21.1. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
21.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
21.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

22. Automatic renewal
22.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
22.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

23. Payment of claims
23.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
23.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

24. Waiver
24.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

25. Premium payment
25.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
25.2. If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
