5.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
5.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
5.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
6.3. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.4. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

15.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.4  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.5  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.6  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.7  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.8  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Customer support
III.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
III.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART IV: Coordination of benefits
IV.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
IV.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART V: Leaving the plan
V.1  Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
V.2  Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

PART VI: Automatic renewal
VI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
VI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART VII: Reasonable precautions
VII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
VII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART VIII: Exchange of information
VIII.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
VIII.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART IX: Cancellation
IX.1  The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
IX.2  After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
IX.3  The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

PART X: Therapy Services
X.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
X.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
X.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
X.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART XI: Records and evidence
XI.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XI.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XII: Cooperation
XII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XIII: Taxes
XIII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XIII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XIV: Accessibility
XIV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XV: Interest
XV.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVI: Sanctions
XVI.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XVII: Premium payment
XVII.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XVII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XVIII: Appeals
XVIII.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
XVIII.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
XVIII.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART XIX: Assignment
XIX.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XX: Dental Care
XX.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
XX.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
XX.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
XX.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
XX.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
XX.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART XXI: Interpretation
XXI.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXI.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXI.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXII: Third-party administrators
XXII.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
XXII.2  Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXIII: Vision Care
XXIII.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
XXIII.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
XXIII.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
XXIII.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART XXIV: Complaints
XXIV.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXIV.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXIV.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXV: Waiver
XXV.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXVI: Optional cover: Hearing Care
XXVI.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
XXVI.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
XXVI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
XXVI.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART XXVII: Wellness allowance
XXVII.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXVII.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXVIII: Claims documents
XXVIII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXVIII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIX: Data protection
XXIX.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXIX.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXIX.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

XXXIII.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

XXXVI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.

XXXVIII.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.

CASE PRESENTATION A
TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.4 Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.5 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
1.6 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.7 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
3.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 4 - TRIP CANCELLATION
4.1 We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
4.5 We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
5.2 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
6.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.3 You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 7 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
7.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
7.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 8 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
8.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
8.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 9 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
9.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
9.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 10 - TAXES
10.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
10.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Tessera Warranty Company
In this policy, "the Provider" means Tessera Warranty Company and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(b) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
(c) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(d) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(d) The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.
(b) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 6. Third-party administrators
(a) The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
(b) Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 7. Electronic documents
(a) The Provider will send documents by email unless the Customer asks for paper copies.
(b) The Customer must tell the Provider if the Customer's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 8. Waiver
(a) If the Provider does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Provider has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 9. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 10. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 11. Compensation scheme
(a) The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 12. Interest
(a) The Provider will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 13. Payment of claims
(a) The Provider will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Customer's name.
(b) The Provider aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Provider needs.

Article 14. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 15. Data protection
(a) The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

Article 16. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 17. Data and backups
(a) The Provider is not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on the Customer's device.
(b) The Customer should back up the Customer's data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

Article 18. Cancellation
(a) The Customer can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Customer can cancel at any time; the Provider will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Provider can cancel this policy by giving the Customer 30 days' written notice to the last address the Provider holds.

Article 19. Repair process
(a) After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
(b) The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

Article 20. Notices

(b) Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

(a) Unless the Customer tells the Provider otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Provider holds.
(b) The Customer can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Provider's helpline.

Article 22. Change of address
(a) The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
(b) The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 23. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Provider may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 24. Renewal
(a) The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 25. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 26. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 27. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3 Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5 Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6 Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7 Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.9 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.10 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.11 Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.12 Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.13 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.14 Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.15 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.16 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.17 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.18 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.19 Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.20 Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.21 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.22 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - DENTAL CARE
3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 4 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
4.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
4.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
4.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 5 - THERAPY SERVICES
5.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
5.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
5.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
5.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 6 - VISION CARE
6.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
6.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
6.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
6.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.2 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.3 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.4 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.5 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
9.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 10 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
10.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
10.2 If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 11 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
11.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
11.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 12 - WELLNESS ALLOWANCE
12.1 Each plan year you may claim up to $150 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
12.2 The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SECTION 13 - COOPERATION
13.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
13.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 14 - INFLATION
14.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
14.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 15 - ARBITRATION
15.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
15.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 16 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
16.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
16.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 17 - SALVAGE
17.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
17.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 18 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
18.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
18.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 19 - OTHER INSURANCE
19.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
19.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 20 - GOVERNING LAW
20.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
20.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 21 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
21.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
21.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 22 - DATA PROTECTION
22.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
22.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
22.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 23 - CANCELLATION
23.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
23.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
23.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 24 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
24.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
24.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 25 - SEVERABILITY
25.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 26 - FRAUD
26.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
26.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 27 - CURRENCY
27.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
27.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 28 - ASSIGNMENT
28.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 29 - SUBROGATION
29.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
29.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 30 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
30.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
30.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 31 - NOTICES
31.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
31.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 32 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
32.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
32.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 33 - COMPLAINTS
33.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
33.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
33.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 34 - RENEWAL
34.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
34.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 35 - INTERPRETATION
35.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
35.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
35.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 36 - APPEALS
36.1 If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
36.2 An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
36.3 We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

SECTION 37 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
37.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
37.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 38 - MARKET CONDITIONS
38.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 39 - DEPENDANTS
39.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
39.2 Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

SECTION 40 - SANCTIONS
40.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 41 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
41.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
41.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 42 - COMMUNICATION
42.1 We will communicate with you in English.
42.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 43 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
43.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
43.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
43.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 44 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
44.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
44.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 45 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
45.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
45.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 46 - TAXES
46.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
46.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 47 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
47.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 48 - LEAVING THE PLAN
48.1 Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
48.2 Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

SECTION 49 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
49.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
49.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 50 - DISCOUNTS
50.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
50.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 51 - COORDINATION OF BENEFITS
51.1 If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
51.2 You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

SECTION 52 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
52.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
52.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 53 - INTEREST
53.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 54 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
54.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
54.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
54.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2 Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.3 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
1.4 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.5 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.6 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.7 Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.8 Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.9 Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
3.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 4 - BAGGAGE AND PERSONAL BELONGINGS
4.1 We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2 The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
4.3 The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5 We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6 We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

SECTION 5 - OPTIONAL COVER: TRAVEL DELAY
5.1 We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
5.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3 We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

SECTION 6 - TRIP CANCELLATION

6.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.

6.4 We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
6.5 We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

8.2 You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Group Health Cash Plan
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.2** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.3** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.4** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.5** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.6** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.7** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.8** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.9** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.10** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.11** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.12** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.13** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.14** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.15** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.16** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.17** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Dental Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **3.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **3.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **3.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 4. Therapy Services
- **4.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **4.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 5. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **5.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **5.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 6. Vision Care
- **6.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **6.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **6.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **7.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.5** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **8.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 9. Dependants
- **9.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **9.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 10. Records and evidence
- **10.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **10.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **10.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 11. Accessibility
- **11.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 12. Appeals
- **12.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **12.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **12.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 13. Assignment
- **13.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 14. Automatic renewal
- **14.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **14.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 15. Duty of fair presentation
- **15.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **15.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **15.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 16. Interpretation
- **16.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **16.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **16.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 17. Severability
- **17.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 18. Compensation scheme
- **18.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **18.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 19. Taxes
- **19.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **19.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 20. Subrogation
- **20.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **20.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 21. Notices
- **21.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **21.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 22. Data protection
- **22.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **22.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **22.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 23. Communication
- **23.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **23.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 24. Premium payment
- **24.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **24.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 25. Renewal
- **25.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **25.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 26. Claims documents
- **26.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **26.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 27. Leaving the plan
- **27.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **27.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 28. Waiver
- **28.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 29. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **29.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 30. Coordination of benefits
- **30.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **30.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 31. Inflation
- **31.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **31.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 32. Currency
- **32.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **32.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 33. Salvage
- **33.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **33.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 34. Geographical limits
- **34.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **34.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 35. Change of address
- **35.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **35.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 36. Changes in circumstances
- **36.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **36.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 37. Wellness allowance
- **37.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **37.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 38. Arbitration
- **38.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **38.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 39. Instalment agreements
- **39.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **39.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 40. How to read this document
- **40.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **40.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **40.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 41. Reasonable precautions
- **41.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **41.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 42. Third-party administrators
- **42.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **42.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 43. Joint policyholders
- **43.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **43.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 44. Other insurance
- **44.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **44.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 45. Electronic documents
- **45.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **45.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **45.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 46. Fraud
- **46.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **46.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 47. Cancellation
- **47.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **47.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
- **47.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 48. Governing law
- **48.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **48.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 49. Sanctions
- **49.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 50. Recovery of costs
- **50.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 51. Environmental commitment
- **51.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **51.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 52. Exchange of information
- **52.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **52.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 53. Discounts
- **53.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **53.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 54. Customer support
- **54.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **54.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 55. Interest
- **55.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 56. Eligibility
- **56.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **56.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 57. Cooperation
- **57.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **57.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 58. Complaints
- **58.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **58.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **58.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 59. Market conditions
- **59.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 60. Payment of claims
- **60.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **60.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

Thanks.

HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(c) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(d) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(e) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(f) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(g) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(h) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(i) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(j) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(k) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(l) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(m) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 4. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 5. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 6. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 7. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 8. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 9. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 10. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 11. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 12. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 13. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 14. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 15. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 16. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 17. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 18. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 19. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 20. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 21. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 22. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 23. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 24. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 25. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 26. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 27. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 28. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 29. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 30. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 31. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 32. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 33. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 34. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 35. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 36. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 37. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 38. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 39. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 40. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

- **2.1** Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.

In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(e) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(f) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(g) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(h) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(i) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(j) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(k) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(l) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(m) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(n) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 6. Flood

+++ b/hackage-docs.sh
@@ -42 +42,47 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+set -e
 
+if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
+  echo "Usage: scripts/hackage-docs.sh HACKAGE_USER"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+user=$1
+
+cabal_file=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -name "*.cabal" -print -quit)
+if [ ! -f "$cabal_file" ]; then
+  echo "Run this script in the top-level package directory"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+pkg=$(awk -F ":[[:space:]]*" 'tolower($1)=="name"    { print $2 }' < "$cabal_file")
+ver=$(awk -F ":[[:space:]]*" 'tolower($1)=="version" { print $2 }' < "$cabal_file")
+
+if [ -z "$pkg" ]; then
+  echo "Unable to determine package name"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+if [ -z "$ver" ]; then
+  echo "Unable to determine package version"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+echo "Detected package: $pkg-$ver"
+
+dir=$(mktemp -d build-docs.XXXXXX)
+trap 'rm -r "$dir"' EXIT
+
+cabal haddock --hoogle --hyperlink-source --html-location='/package/$pkg-$version/docs' --contents-location='/package/$pkg-$version' --haddock-options="--hyperlinked-source"
+
+cp -R dist/doc/html/$pkg/ $dir/$pkg-$ver-docs
+
+tar cvz -C $dir --format=ustar -f $dir/$pkg-$ver-docs.tar.gz $pkg-$ver-docs
+
+curl -X PUT \
+     -H 'Content-Type: application/x-tar' \
+     -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
+     -u "$user" \
+     --data-binary "@$dir/$pkg-$ver-docs.tar.gz" \
+     "https://hackage.haskell.org/package/$pkg-$ver/docs"
+
