TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(e) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(f) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(g) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(h) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(i) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(j) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(k) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(l) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(m) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(n) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(o) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(p) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(q) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(r) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(s) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(t) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 6. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 10. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 11. Missed departure
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

Article 12. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 13. Cooperation
(a) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 14. Change of address
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 15. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 16. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 17. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 18. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 19. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 20. Repatriation
(a) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(b) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

Article 21. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 22. Records and evidence
(a) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 23. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 24. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 25. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

# Staff Health Reimbursement Plan Rules
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.2** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.3** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.4** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.5** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.6** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.7** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.8** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.9** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.10** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.11** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.12** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.15** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.16** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Sanctions
- **3.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 4. Therapy Services
- **4.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **4.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 5. Dependants
- **5.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **5.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 6. Exchange of information
- **6.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **6.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 7. Recovery of costs
- **7.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 8. Accessibility
- **8.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 9. Dental Care
- **9.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **9.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **9.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **9.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **9.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **9.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 10. Discounts
- **10.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **10.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 11. Severability
- **11.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 12. Payment of claims
- **12.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **12.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 13. Claims documents
- **13.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **13.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 14. Records and evidence
- **14.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **14.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **14.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 15. Other insurance
- **15.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **15.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 16. Reasonable precautions
- **16.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **16.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

+#!/bin/bash
+set -e
 
+if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
+  echo "Usage: scripts/hackage-docs.sh HACKAGE_USER"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+user=$1
+
+cabal_file=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -name "*.cabal" -print -quit)
+if [ ! -f "$cabal_file" ]; then
+  echo "Run this script in the top-level package directory"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+pkg=$(awk -F ":[[:space:]]*" 'tolower($1)=="name"    { print $2 }' < "$cabal_file")
+ver=$(awk -F ":[[:space:]]*" 'tolower($1)=="version" { print $2 }' < "$cabal_file")
+
+if [ -z "$pkg" ]; then
+  echo "Unable to determine package name"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+if [ -z "$ver" ]; then
+  echo "Unable to determine package version"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+echo "Detected package: $pkg-$ver"
+
+dir=$(mktemp -d build-docs.XXXXXX)
+trap 'rm -r "$dir"' EXIT
+
+cabal haddock --hoogle --hyperlink-source --html-location='/package/$pkg-$version/docs' --contents-location='/package/$pkg-$version' --haddock-options="--hyperlinked-source"
+
+cp -R dist/doc/html/$pkg/ $dir/$pkg-$ver-docs
+
+tar cvz -C $dir --format=ustar -f $dir/$pkg-$ver-docs.tar.gz $pkg-$ver-docs
+

+     -H 'Content-Type: application/x-tar' \
+     -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.6** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.7** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.8** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.9** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.10** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
- **1.11** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.12** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.13** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.14** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.17** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.18** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.19** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.20** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
- **1.21** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Changes in circumstances
- **3.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **3.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 4. Assignment
- **4.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 5. Interpretation
- **5.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **5.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **5.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 6. Repatriation
- **6.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **6.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 7. Communication
- **7.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **7.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 8. Inflation
- **8.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **8.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 9. Payment of claims
- **9.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **9.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 10. Salvage
- **10.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **10.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 11. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **11.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **11.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
- **11.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **11.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **11.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **11.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 12. Discounts
- **12.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **12.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 13. Data protection
- **13.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **13.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **13.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 14. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **14.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **14.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **14.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **14.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **14.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **14.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 15. Trip Cancellation
- **15.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **15.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **15.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **15.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **15.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 16. Premium payment
- **16.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **16.2** If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 17. Market conditions
- **17.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 18. Currency
- **18.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **18.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 19. Electronic documents
- **19.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **19.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **19.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 20. Other insurance
- **20.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **20.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 21. Personal liability
- **21.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **21.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **21.3** The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 22. Third-party administrators
- **22.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **22.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 23. Cooperation
- **23.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **23.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 24. Customer support
- **24.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **24.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 25. Accessibility
- **25.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 26. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **26.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **26.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **26.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 27. General exclusions
- **27.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **27.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **27.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 28. Instalment agreements
- **28.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **28.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 29. Missed departure
- **29.1** We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
- **29.2** You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

## 30. Subrogation
- **30.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **30.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 31. Notices
- **31.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **31.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 32. Geographical limits
- **32.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **32.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 33. How to read this document
- **33.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **33.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **33.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 34. Waiver
- **34.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 35. Governing law
- **35.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **35.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 36. Making a claim
- **36.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **36.2** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **36.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

state.policy:
EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.4  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.5  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.6  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.7  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.8  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Customer support
III.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
III.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART IV: Coordination of benefits
IV.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
IV.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART V: Leaving the plan
V.1  Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
V.2  Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

PART VI: Automatic renewal
VI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
VI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART VII: Reasonable precautions
VII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
VII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART VIII: Exchange of information
VIII.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
VIII.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART IX: Cancellation
IX.1  The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
IX.2  After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
IX.3  The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

PART X: Therapy Services
X.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
X.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
X.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
X.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART XI: Records and evidence
XI.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XI.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XII: Cooperation
XII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XIII: Taxes
XIII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XIII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XIV: Accessibility
XIV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XV: Interest
XV.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVI: Sanctions
XVI.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XVII: Premium payment
XVII.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XVII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XVIII: Appeals
XVIII.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
XVIII.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
XVIII.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART XIX: Assignment
XIX.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XX: Dental Care
XX.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
XX.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
XX.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
XX.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
XX.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
XX.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART XXI: Interpretation
XXI.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXI.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXI.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXII: Third-party administrators
XXII.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
XXII.2  Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXIII: Vision Care
XXIII.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
XXIII.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
XXIII.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
XXIII.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART XXIV: Complaints
XXIV.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXIV.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXIV.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXV: Waiver
XXV.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXVI: Optional cover: Hearing Care
XXVI.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
XXVI.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
XXVI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
XXVI.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART XXVII: Wellness allowance
XXVII.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXVII.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXVIII: Claims documents
XXVIII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXVIII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIX: Data protection
XXIX.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXIX.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXIX.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART XXX: Electronic documents
XXX.1  The Plan will send documents by email unless the Member asks for paper copies.
XXX.2  The Member must tell the Plan if the Member's email address changes.
XXX.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXXI: Compensation scheme
XXXI.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXXI.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXXII: Fraud
XXXII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXII.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIII: Recovery of costs
XXXIII.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXXIV: Market conditions
XXXIV.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XXXV: Notices
XXXV.1  Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
XXXV.2  Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXXVI: Joint policyholders
XXXVI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XXXVI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XXXVII: Change of address
XXXVII.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXXVII.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXXVIII: Eligibility
XXXVIII.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
XXXVIII.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

PART XXXIX: Geographical limits
XXXIX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XXXIX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XXXX: General exclusions
XXXX.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
XXXX.2  The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XXXX.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXXX.4  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXXX.5  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

PART XXXXI: Currency
XXXXI.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXXXI.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXXXII: Changes in circumstances
XXXXII.1  The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXXXII.2  The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XXXXIII: Making a claim
XXXXIII.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XXXXIII.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXXXIII.3  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART XXXXIV: Inflation
XXXXIV.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXXIV.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXXV: Other insurance
XXXXV.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
XXXXV.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

PART XXXXVI: Subrogation
XXXXVI.1  The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXXXVI.2  The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXXXVII: Governing law
XXXXVII.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXXXVII.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXXXVIII: Duty of fair presentation
XXXXVIII.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XXXXVIII.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXXXVIII.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXXXIX: Payment of claims
XXXXIX.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
XXXXIX.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XXXXX: Discounts
XXXXX.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXXXX.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Plan may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3. Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.4. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.5. Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.6. Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.7. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.8. High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.9. Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.10. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.11. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.12. Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.15. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.19. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.20. Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Sanctions
3.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

4. How to read this document
4.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
4.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
4.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

5. Change of address
5.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
5.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

6. Geographical limits
6.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
6.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

7. Interest
7.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

8. Subrogation
8.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
8.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

9. Governing law
9.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
9.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

10. Communication
10.1. We will communicate with you in English.
10.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

11. Alternative accommodation
11.1. If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
11.2. We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
11.3. Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

12. Assignment
12.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

13. Contents temporarily removed
13.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
13.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

14. Automatic renewal
14.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.

15. Tenant's improvements
15.1. If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.

16. Electronic documents
16.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
16.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
16.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

17. Severability
17.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

18. Salvage
18.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.

19. Waiver
19.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

20.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.

21.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.

22. Reasonable precautions
22.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.

23. Compensation scheme
23.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.

24.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.

TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.4. Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.5. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
1.6. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.7. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.8. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.9. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.10. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.11. Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.12. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
1.13. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.14. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.15. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Joint policyholders
3.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
3.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

4. Cooperation
4.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
4.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

5. Accessibility
5.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

6. Salvage
6.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
6.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

7. Sanctions
7.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

8. Instalment agreements
8.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
8.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

9. Market conditions
9.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

10. Geographical limits
10.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
10.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

11. Environmental commitment
11.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
11.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

12. Changes in circumstances
12.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
12.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

13. Complaints
13.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
13.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
13.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

14. Rental car excess
14.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
14.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

15. Renewal
15.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
15.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

16. Governing law
16.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
16.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

17. Duty of fair presentation
17.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
17.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
17.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

18. Communication
18.1. We will communicate with you in English.
18.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

19. Compensation scheme
19.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
19.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

20. Waiver
20.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

21. Baggage and Personal Belongings
21.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
21.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
21.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
21.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
21.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
21.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

22. Electronic documents
22.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
22.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
22.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

23. Emergency assistance
23.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
23.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
23.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

24. Optional cover: Travel Delay
24.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
24.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
24.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

25. Missed departure
25.1. We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
25.2. You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

26. Interpretation
26.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
26.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
26.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

27. Data protection
27.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
27.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
27.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

28. Records and evidence
28.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
28.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
28.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

29. Claims documents
29.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
29.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

30. Automatic renewal
30.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
30.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

31. Trip Cancellation
31.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
31.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
31.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
31.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
31.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

32. Emergency Medical Expenses
32.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
32.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
32.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
32.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
32.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
32.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

33. How to read this document
33.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
33.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
33.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

34. Change of address
34.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
34.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

35. Notices
35.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
35.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

36. Severability
36.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

37. Third-party administrators
37.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
37.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

38. Exchange of information
38.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
38.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

39. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
39.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

40. Customer support
40.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
40.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

41. Repatriation
41.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
41.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

42. Fraud
42.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
42.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

43. Personal liability
43.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
43.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
43.3. The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

44. Subrogation
44.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
44.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

45. Other insurance
45.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
45.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

46. Interest
46.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

47. Inflation
47.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
47.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

48. Taxes
48.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
48.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

49. Legal expenses abroad
49.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
49.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

50. Recovery of costs
50.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

51. Discounts
51.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
51.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

52. General exclusions
52.1. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
52.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
52.3. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

53. Assignment
53.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

54. Payment of claims
54.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
54.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

55. Arbitration
55.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
55.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

56. Cancellation
56.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
56.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
56.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

57. Making a claim
57.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
57.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
57.3. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

58. Currency
58.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
58.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

59. Reasonable precautions
59.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
59.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

60. Premium payment
60.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
60.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.
