state.policy:
HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(f) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(g) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(h) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(i) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(j) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(k) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(l) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(m) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(n) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(o) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 5. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 6. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 10. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 11. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 12. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 13. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 14. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 15. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 16. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 17. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 18. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 19. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 20. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 21. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 22. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 23. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 24. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 25. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 26. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 27. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 28. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 29. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 30. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 31. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 32. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 33. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 34. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 35. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 36. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 37. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 38. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS

2.1 Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.

2.5 The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

4.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

5.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.

7.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.

(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.

(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.

(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.

(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 52. Exchange of information

(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 53. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 54. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 55. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 56. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 57. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 58. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 59. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 60. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.3. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Escape of Water
3.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
3.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
3.3. We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
3.4. We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

4. Flood
4.1. We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
4.3. The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

5. General exclusions
5.1. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
5.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
5.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

6. Making a claim
6.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
6.2. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

7. Interpretation
7.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
7.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
7.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

8. Data protection
8.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
8.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
8.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

9. Customer support
9.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
9.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

10. Interest
10.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

11. Exchange of information
11.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
11.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

12. Taxes
12.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
12.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

13. Changes in circumstances
13.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
13.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

14. Environmental commitment
14.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
14.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

15. Cooperation
15.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
15.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

16. Inflation
16.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
16.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

17. Compensation scheme
17.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
17.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

18. Arbitration
18.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
18.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

19. Garden and outdoor cover
19.1. We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
19.2. We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Agent: Sure. When did the policy start and what covers does your schedule show?
Customer (Maya): It started on Sunday, March 23, 2025. The schedule lists Theft, Escape of Water, Flood, and extensions: none.
Agent: When did the incident happen, and what happened?
Customer (Maya): On Thursday, April 10, 2025. Heavy rain caused the nearby river to burst its banks and flood the street.
Agent: Anything else we should know?
Customer (Maya): Maya works from home three days a week. A neighbour reported the incident to the building manager. The building is a converted warehouse with six flats.
Agent: Noted. I am logging this claim today, Friday, April 18, 2025, the first time it has been reported to us. Our adjuster has assessed the loss at $1,909.99.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.2** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.3** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. How to read this document
- **3.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **3.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **3.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 4. Exchange of information
- **4.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **4.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 5. Complaints
- **5.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **5.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **5.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 6. Rental car excess
- **6.1** If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
- **6.2** This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

## 7. Trip Cancellation
- **7.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **7.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **7.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **7.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **7.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 8. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **8.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **8.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **8.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 9. Communication
- **9.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **9.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 10. Legal expenses abroad
- **10.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **10.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 11. Salvage
- **11.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **11.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 12. General exclusions
- **12.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **12.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 13. Claims documents
- **13.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **13.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 14. Making a claim
- **14.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **14.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **14.3** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Northstar Underwriting
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Northstar Underwriting and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(e) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(f) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(g) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
(h) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(i) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
(j) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(k) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(l) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(m) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(n) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 6. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 10. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

Article 11. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 12. Cooperation
(a) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 13. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 14. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
(b) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 15. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 16. Premium payment
(a) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 17. Records and evidence
(a) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 18. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 19. Cancellation
(a) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 20. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 21. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 22. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 23. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 24. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 25. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 26. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

Article 27. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 28. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Insured Person's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Insured Person's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 29. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 30. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 31. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 32. Missed departure
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

Article 33. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 34. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.

Issued by Lantern General Insurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.3  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.4  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.5  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.6  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.7  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.8  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.9  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.10  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.11  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.12  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.13  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART VI: Escape of Water
VI.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART IX: Discounts
IX.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
IX.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART X: Interest
X.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XI: Garden and outdoor cover
XI.1  The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
XI.2  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

PART XII: Interpretation
XII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XII.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XII.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XIII: Alternative accommodation
XIII.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
XIII.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
XIII.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART XIV: Premium payment
XIV.1  The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XIV.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XV: Changes in circumstances
XV.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XV.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XVI: Data protection
XVI.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XVI.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XVI.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XVII: Contents temporarily removed
XVII.1  The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
XVII.2  Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

PART XVIII: Duty of fair presentation
XVIII.1  The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
XVIII.2  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XVIII.3  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XIX: Salvage
XIX.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XIX.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XX: Automatic renewal
XX.1  Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XX.2  The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XXI: Notices
XXI.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
XXI.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXII: Records and evidence
XXII.1  The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXII.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXIII: Recovery of costs
XXIII.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XXIV: How to read this document
XXIV.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XXIV.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XXIV.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XXV: Compensation scheme
XXV.1  The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXV.2  If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXVI: Market conditions
XXVI.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XXVII: Change of address
XXVII.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
XXVII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXVIII: Assignment
XXVIII.1  The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

PART XXIX: Communication
XXIX.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
XXIX.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXX: Tenant's improvements
XXX.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
XXX.2  This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

PART XXXI: Payment of claims
XXXI.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XXXI.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XXXII: Cooperation
XXXII.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXXII.2  The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART XXXIII: Claims documents
XXXIII.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XXXIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIV: Exchange of information
XXXIV.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
XXXIV.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

PART XXXV: Renewal
XXXV.1  The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XXXV.2  The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XXXVI: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXXVI.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXXVII: Cancellation
XXXVII.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XXXVII.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
XXXVII.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XXXVIII: Subrogation
XXXVIII.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXXVIII.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXXIX: Inflation
XXXIX.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXIX.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXX: Governing law
XXXX.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXXX.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXXXI: Complaints
XXXXI.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXXXI.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXXXI.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXXXII: Other insurance
XXXXII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XXXXII.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

PART XXXXIII: Waiver
XXXXIII.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXXXIV: Environmental commitment
XXXXIV.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXXXIV.2  The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXXXV: Taxes
XXXXV.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XXXXV.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXXXVI: Accessibility
XXXXVI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXXXVII: Electronic documents
XXXXVII.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
XXXXVII.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
XXXXVII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXXXVIII: Locks and keys
XXXXVIII.1  If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
XXXXVIII.2  The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $750 for any one claim.

PART XXXXIX: Joint policyholders
XXXXIX.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XXXXIX.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XXXXX: Currency
XXXXX.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXXXX.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXXXXI: Third-party administrators
XXXXXI.1  The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
XXXXXI.2  Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXXXXII: Freezer contents
XXXXXII.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
XXXXXII.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART XXXXXIII: Sanctions
XXXXXIII.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXXXXIV: Fraud
XXXXXIV.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXXXIV.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXXXV: Severability
XXXXXV.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XXXXXVI: Arbitration
XXXXXVI.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XXXXXVI.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

PART XXXXXVII: Instalment agreements
XXXXXVII.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXXXXVII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXXXXVIII: Customer support
XXXXXVIII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXXXXVIII.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART XXXXXIX: Geographical limits
XXXXXIX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XXXXXIX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XXXXXX: Reasonable precautions
XXXXXX.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXXXXX.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.6  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.7  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.8  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.9  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.10  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.11  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.12  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.13  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.14  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.19  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.20  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Claims documents
III.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
III.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART IV: Salvage
IV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
IV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART V: Complaints
V.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
V.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
V.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART VI: Governing law
VI.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
VI.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART VII: Sanctions
VII.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART VIII: Theft
VIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
VIII.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
VIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
VIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
VIII.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
VIII.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IX: Freezer contents
IX.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
IX.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART X: Records and evidence
X.1  The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
X.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
X.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XI: Alternative accommodation
XI.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
XI.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
XI.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART XII: Cooperation
XII.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
XII.2  The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART XIII: Interest
XIII.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XIV: Escape of Water
XIV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
XIV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XIV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
XIV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART XV: Data protection
XV.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XV.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XV.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XVI: Garden and outdoor cover
XVI.1  The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
XVI.2  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

PART XVII: Accessibility
XVII.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XVIII: Joint policyholders
XVIII.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XVIII.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XIX: How to read this document
XIX.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XIX.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XIX.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XX: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
XX.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
XX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
XX.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
XX.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
XX.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART XXI: Third-party administrators
XXI.1  The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
XXI.2  Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXII: Interpretation
XXII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXII.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXII.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXIII: Flood
XXIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
XXIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XXIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XXIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XXIV: General exclusions
XXIV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXIV.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXIV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART XXV: Subrogation
XXV.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXV.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXVI: Communication
XXVI.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
XXVI.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXVII: Locks and keys
XXVII.1  If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
XXVII.2  The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

PART XXVIII: Change of address
XXVIII.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
XXVIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXIX: Currency
XXIX.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXIX.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXX: Inflation
XXX.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXX.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXI: Tenant's improvements
XXXI.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
XXXI.2  This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

PART XXXII: Arbitration
XXXII.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XXXII.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

PART XXXIII: Fraud
XXXIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIV: Payment of claims
XXXIV.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XXXIV.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XXXV: Market conditions
XXXV.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XXXVI: Contents temporarily removed
XXXVI.1  The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
XXXVI.2  Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

PART XXXVII: Taxes
XXXVII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XXXVII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXXVIII: Premium payment
XXXVIII.1  The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXXVIII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXXIX: Waiver
XXXIX.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXXX: Reasonable precautions
XXXX.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXXX.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXXXI: Compensation scheme
XXXXI.1  The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXXXI.2  If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXXXII: Environmental commitment
XXXXII.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXXXII.2  The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXXXIII: Customer support
XXXXIII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXXXIII.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART XXXXIV: Severability
XXXXIV.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XXXXV: Instalment agreements
XXXXV.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXXXV.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXXXVI: Recovery of costs
XXXXVI.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XXXXVII: Other insurance
XXXXVII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XXXXVII.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

PART XXXXVIII: Automatic renewal
XXXXVIII.1  Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XXXXVIII.2  The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XXXXIX: Assignment
XXXXIX.1  The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

PART XXXXX: Making a claim
XXXXX.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XXXXX.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXXXX.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART XXXXXI: Duty of fair presentation
XXXXXI.1  The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
XXXXXI.2  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXXXXI.3  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXXXXII: Electronic documents
XXXXXII.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
XXXXXII.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
XXXXXII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
