I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.5  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.6  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.7  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.8  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.9  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.10  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.11  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.12  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.13  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.14  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.15  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART VI: Escape of Water
VI.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART IX: Interpretation
IX.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
IX.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
IX.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART X: Subrogation
X.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
X.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XI: Taxes
XI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XII: Data protection
XII.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XII.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XII.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XIII: Change of address
XIII.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
XIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XIV: Currency
XIV.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XIV.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XV: Renewal
XV.1  The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XV.2  The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XVI: Assignment
XVI.1  The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

PART XVII: Salvage
XVII.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XVII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

XVIII.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXI: Locks and keys

PART XXII: Notices
XXII.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
XXII.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXIII: Sanctions

PART XXIV: Tenant's improvements

PART XXV: Cooperation
XXV.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Compass Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.2** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.3** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
- **1.4** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.5** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.6** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.7** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.8** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.9** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.10** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.11** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.12** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.13** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.14** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.15** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.16** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.17** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Fraud
- **4.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **4.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 5. Other insurance
- **5.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **5.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 6. Notices
- **6.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **6.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 7. Accessibility
- **7.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 8. Exchange of information
- **8.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **8.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 9. Personal liability
- **9.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **9.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **9.3** The most we will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 10. Subrogation
- **10.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **10.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 11. Interpretation
- **11.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **11.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **11.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 12. Assignment
- **12.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 13. Premium payment
- **13.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **13.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 14. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **14.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **14.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
- **14.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **14.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **14.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **14.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 15. Recovery of costs
- **15.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 16. Compensation scheme
- **16.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **16.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 17. Change of address
- **17.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **17.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 18. Payment of claims
- **18.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **18.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 19. Sanctions
- **19.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 20. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **20.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **20.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **20.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 21. Discounts
- **21.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **21.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 22. Cancellation
- **22.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **22.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **22.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 23. Trip Cancellation
- **23.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **23.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
- **23.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **23.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **23.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 24. Repatriation
- **24.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **24.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 25. Changes in circumstances
- **25.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **25.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 26. Geographical limits
- **26.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **26.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 27. General exclusions
- **27.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **27.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **27.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **27.4** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 28. Electronic documents
- **28.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **28.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **28.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 29. Records and evidence
- **29.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **29.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **29.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 30. Waiver
- **30.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 31. Salvage
- **31.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **31.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 32. Claims documents
- **32.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **32.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 33. Currency
- **33.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **33.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 34. Communication
- **34.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **34.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 35. Joint policyholders
- **35.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **35.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 36. Taxes
- **36.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **36.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 37. Reasonable precautions
- **37.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **37.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 38. Emergency assistance
- **38.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **38.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **38.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 39. Environmental commitment
- **39.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **39.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 40. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **40.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 41. Instalment agreements
- **41.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **41.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 42. Data protection
- **42.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **42.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **42.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 43. Interest
- **43.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 44. Rental car excess
- **44.1** If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
- **44.2** This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

## 45. Arbitration
- **45.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **45.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 46. Making a claim
- **46.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **46.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **46.3** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 47. Legal expenses abroad
- **47.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **47.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 48. How to read this document
- **48.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **48.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **48.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 49. Severability
- **49.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Electronics Care Plan
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.4** Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
- **1.5** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.6** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.7** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.8** Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
- **1.9** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
- **1.12** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.15** Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
- **1.16** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.17** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Governing law
- **3.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **3.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 4. Accidental Damage
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **4.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 5. Change of address
- **5.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **5.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 6. Breakdown
- **6.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **6.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **6.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 7. Claims documents
- **7.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **7.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 8. Sanctions
- **8.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 9. Third-party administrators
- **9.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **9.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 10. Interest
- **10.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 11. Premium payment
- **11.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **11.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 12. Waiver
- **12.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 13. Other insurance
- **13.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **13.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 14. Transferring the plan
- **14.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **14.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 15. Data protection
- **15.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **15.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **15.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 16. Data and backups
- **16.1** We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
- **16.2** You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

## 17. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **17.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **17.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **17.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **17.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **17.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 18. Exchange of information
- **18.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **18.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 19. Duty of fair presentation
- **19.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **19.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **19.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 20. Changes in circumstances
- **20.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **20.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 21. General exclusions
- **21.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **21.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **21.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **21.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **21.5** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 22. Customer support
- **22.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **22.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 23. Payment of claims
- **23.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **23.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 24. Taxes
- **24.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **24.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 25. Making a claim
- **25.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **25.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **25.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 26. Subrogation
- **26.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **26.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 27. Salvage
- **27.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **27.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Oakfield Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Oakfield Assurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(c) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(d) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(e) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(f) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(g) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(h) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(i) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(j) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(k) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(l) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(m) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 6. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 10. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 11. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 12. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 13. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 14. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 15. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 16. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 17. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 18. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 19. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 20. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 21. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 22. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 23. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 24. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 25. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 26. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.6** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.7** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.10** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.11** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.12** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.13** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.14** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.15** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.16** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.17** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.18** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.19** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.20** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.21** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.22** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.

SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.2. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.3. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.4. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Trip Cancellation
3.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
3.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

4. Cancellation
4.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
4.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
4.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

5. Claims documents
5.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
5.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

6. Accessibility
6.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

7. Baggage and Personal Belongings
7.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
7.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
7.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
7.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
7.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
7.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

8. Severability
8.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

9. Instalment agreements
9.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
9.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

10. Rental car excess
10.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
10.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

11. General exclusions
11.1. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
11.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

12. Making a claim
12.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
12.2. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
12.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

13. Joint policyholders
13.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
13.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

14. Repatriation
14.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
14.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

15. Electronic documents
15.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
15.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
15.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

16. Complaints
16.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
16.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
16.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

17. Currency
17.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
17.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

18. Exchange of information
18.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
18.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.3** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.4** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.7** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.8** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.9** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.12** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.15** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.16** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Flood
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 4. Escape of Water
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **4.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **4.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Theft
- **6.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **6.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.

- **16.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

- **22.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

- **38.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

- **39.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.

- **43.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.

- **44.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **44.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

- **45.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **45.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

- **46.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.

- **47.1** We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.

- **48.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

- **50.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.

- **50.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

- **51.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

In this policy, "the Provider" means Tessera Warranty Company and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

(j) Limit means the most the Provider will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(k) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
(l) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
(m) Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

(r) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(f) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(g) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(h) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(i) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(j) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(k) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(l) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(m) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(n) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(o) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(p) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(q) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(r) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 4. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 5. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 6. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 10. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 11. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 12. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 13. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 14. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 15. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 16. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 17. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 18. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 19. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 20. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 21. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 22. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 23. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 24. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 25. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 26. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 27. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 28. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 29. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 30. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 31. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 32. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 33. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 34. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 35. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 36. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 37. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 38. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 39. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 40. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 41. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 42. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 43. Locks and keys
(a) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

Article 44. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 45. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 46. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 47. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 48. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 49. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 50. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 51. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 52. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 53. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 54. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 55. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 56. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 57. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 58. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 59. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.

(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

Article 8. Leaving the plan
(a) Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
(b) Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

Article 9. Duty of fair presentation
