CASE PRESENTATION B
# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.4** Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
- **1.5** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.6** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.7** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.8** Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
- **1.9** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.10** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.11** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.12** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.13** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.14** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.15** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.16** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.17** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.18** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.19** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Changes in circumstances
- **3.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **3.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 4. Recovery of costs
- **4.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 5. Renewal
- **5.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **5.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 6. Breakdown
- **6.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **6.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **6.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 7. Automatic renewal
- **7.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **7.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 8. Third-party administrators
- **8.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **8.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 9. Joint policyholders
- **9.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **9.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 10. Discounts
- **10.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **10.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 11. Fraud
- **11.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **11.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 12. How to read this document
- **12.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **12.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **12.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 13. Data protection
- **13.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **13.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **13.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 14. Severability
- **14.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 15. Accessibility
- **15.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 16. Accidental Damage
- **16.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **16.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **16.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **16.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **16.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 17. Transferring the plan
- **17.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **17.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 18. Sanctions
- **18.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 19. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **19.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **19.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **19.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **19.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **19.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 20. Electronic documents
- **20.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **20.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **20.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 21. Notices
- **21.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **21.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 22. Communication
- **22.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **22.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 23. General exclusions
- **23.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **23.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **23.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 24. Replacement devices
- **24.1** If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
- **24.2** Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
- **24.3** Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

## 25. Environmental commitment
- **25.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **25.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 26. Subrogation
- **26.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **26.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 27. Waiver
- **27.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 28. Currency
- **28.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **28.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 29. Cancellation
- **29.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **29.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
- **29.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 30. Reasonable precautions
- **30.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **30.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 31. Repair process
- **31.1** After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
- **31.2** We aim to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

## 32. Making a claim
- **32.1** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **32.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **32.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.4  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.5  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.6  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.7  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.8  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.17  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Hearing Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART IV: Therapy Services
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART V: Vision Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART VI: Dental Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
VI.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
VI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
VI.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
VI.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
VI.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART IX: Geographical limits
IX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
IX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART X: Reasonable precautions
X.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
X.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XI: Environmental commitment
XI.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XI.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XII: Severability
XII.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XIII: Customer support
XIII.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XIII.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART XIV: Payment of claims
XIV.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
XIV.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XV: Interpretation
XV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XVI: Automatic renewal
XVI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XVI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XVII: Waiver
XVII.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

state.policy:
DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Tessera Warranty Company

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
I.2  Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
I.3  Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by the Provider.
I.4  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.5  Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
I.6  Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
I.7  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.8  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
I.9  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
I.10  Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.11  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.12  Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
I.13  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Customer's details, the covers the Customer bought and any extensions.
I.14  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.15  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
III.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
III.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
III.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
III.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART IV: Accidental Damage
IV.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
IV.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IV.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
IV.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
IV.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART V: Breakdown
V.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
V.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
V.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.
VI.2  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.
VI.3  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.4  The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.5  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.6  The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VIII: Transferring the plan
VIII.1  The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
VIII.2  The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

PART IX: Market conditions
IX.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Provider will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART X: Severability
X.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XI: Environmental commitment
XI.1  Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XI.2  The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XII: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XII.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XIII: Software support
XIII.1  The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
XIII.2  Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

PART XIV: Joint policyholders
XIV.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XIV.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XV: Duty of fair presentation
XV.1  The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
XV.2  If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XV.3  If the Customer gives incorrect information carelessly, the Provider may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XVI: Recovery of costs
XVI.1  If the Provider pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Provider may ask the Customer to repay the amount.

PART XVII: Salvage
XVII.1  When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
XVII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

PART XVIII: Inflation
XVIII.1  The Provider may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XVIII.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Customer's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XIX: Exchange of information
XIX.1  To prevent fraud, the Provider may check the details the Customer gives against public records and industry databases.
XIX.2  The Provider may contact previous insurers to confirm the Customer's claims history.

PART XX: Taxes
XX.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XX.2  If the tax rate changes, the Provider may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXI: Sanctions
XXI.1  The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXII: Currency
XXII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXIII: Change of address
XXIII.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
XXIII.2  The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXIV: Accessibility
XXIV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXV: Customer support
XXV.1  The Provider's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXV.2  Outside these hours the Customer can leave a message and the Provider will call back on the next working day.

PART XXVI: Records and evidence
XXVI.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXVI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXVI.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXVII: Electronic documents
XXVII.1  The Provider will send documents by email unless the Customer asks for paper copies.
XXVII.2  The Customer must tell the Provider if the Customer's email address changes.
XXVII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXVIII: Repair process
XXVIII.1  After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
XXVIII.2  The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

PART XXIX: Other insurance
XXIX.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Provider will pay only the Provider's proportionate share.
XXIX.2  The Customer must tell the Provider about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Customer makes a claim.

PART XXX: Unrecoverable devices
XXX.1  If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
XXX.2  The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

PART XXXI: Discounts
XXXI.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXXI.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XXXII: Fraud
XXXII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXII.2  The Provider may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIII: Claims documents
XXXIII.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
XXXIII.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIV: Reasonable precautions
XXXIV.1  The Customer must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXXIV.2  The Customer must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXXV: Interpretation
XXXV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXXV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXXV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXXVI: Data protection
XXXVI.1  The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXXVI.2  The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXXVI.3  The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

PART XXXVII: Assignment
XXXVII.1  The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

PART XXXVIII: Cooperation
XXXVIII.1  The Customer must give the Provider all the help and information the Provider reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXXVIII.2  The Customer must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Provider's written permission.

PART XXXIX: Notices
XXXIX.1  Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
XXXIX.2  Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXXX: Data and backups
XXXX.1  The Provider is not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on the Customer's device.
XXXX.2  The Customer should back up the Customer's data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

PART XXXXI: Third-party administrators
XXXXI.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
XXXXI.2  Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXXXII: Premium payment
XXXXII.1  The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXXXII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXXXIII: Geographical limits
XXXXIII.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XXXXIII.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XXXXIV: Complaints
XXXXIV.1  If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXXXIV.2  The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXXXIV.3  If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXXXV: Compensation scheme
XXXXV.1  The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXXXV.2  If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXXXVI: Replacement devices
XXXXVI.1  If the Provider cannot repair the Customer's device economically, the Provider will replace it with a replacement device.
XXXXVI.2  Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
XXXXVI.3  Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7. Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.9. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.10. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.11. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.12. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.13. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.14. Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.15. Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.16. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.17. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Therapy Services
3.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
3.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
3.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
3.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

4. Vision Care
4.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
4.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
4.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
4.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

5. Optional cover: Hearing Care
5.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
5.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

6. Dental Care
6.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
6.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
6.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
6.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
6.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
6.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.5. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

8. Making a claim
8.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3. You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

9. Salvage
9.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
9.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

10. Wellness allowance
10.1. Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
10.2. The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

11. Electronic documents
11.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
11.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
11.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

12. Change of address
12.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
12.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

13. Renewal
13.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
13.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

14. Taxes
14.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
14.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

15. Leaving the plan
15.1. Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
15.2. Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

16. Sanctions
16.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

17. Interest
17.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

18. Severability
18.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

19. Cooperation
19.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
19.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

20. Coordination of benefits
20.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
20.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

21. Governing law
21.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
21.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

22. Inflation
22.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
22.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

23. Complaints
23.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
23.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
23.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

24. Communication
24.1. We will communicate with you in English.
24.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

25. Interpretation
25.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
25.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
25.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

26. Automatic renewal
26.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
26.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

27. How to read this document
27.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
27.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
27.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

28. Geographical limits
28.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
28.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

29. Duty of fair presentation
29.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
29.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
29.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

30. Environmental commitment
30.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
30.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

31. Discounts
31.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
31.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

32. Subrogation
32.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
32.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

33. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
33.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

34. Changes in circumstances
34.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
34.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

35. Cancellation
35.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
35.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
35.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

36. Customer support
36.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
36.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

37. Appeals
37.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
37.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
37.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

38. Compensation scheme
38.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
38.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

39. Eligibility
39.1. Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
39.2. Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(b) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(c) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(d) Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(e) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(f) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(g) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(h) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(i) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
(j) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(k) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(l) Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
(m) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.
(n) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Payment of claims
(a) The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
(b) The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

Article 4. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 5. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 6. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 7. Waiver
(a) If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 8. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 9. Salvage
(a) When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

Article 10. Records and evidence
(a) The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 11. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 12. Sanctions
(a) The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 13. Dependants
(a) The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
(b) Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

Article 14. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 15. Coordination of benefits
(a) If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
(b) The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

Article 16. Cancellation
(a) The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

Article 17. Notices
(a) Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
(b) Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 18. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
(b) The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

Article 19. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 20. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 21. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 22. Cooperation
(a) The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

Article 23. Compensation scheme
(a) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 24. Premium payment
(a) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 25. Inflation
(a) The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 26. Change of address
(a) The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
(b) The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 27. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 28. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 29. Interest
(a) The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 30. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 31. Data protection
(a) The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

Article 32. Customer support
(a) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

Article 33. Vision Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(d) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

Article 34. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 35. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(d) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(e) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 36. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 37. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
(b) If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 38. Assignment
(a) The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

Article 39. Third-party administrators
(a) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(b) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 40. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

Article 41. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 42. Eligibility
(a) Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
(b) Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

Article 43. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 44. Complaints
(a) If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 45. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 46. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

Issued by Brightline Device Cover
In this policy, "the Provider" means Brightline Device Cover and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

(e) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(f) Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
(g) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(h) Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
(i) Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
(j) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(k) Limit means the most the Provider will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(l) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
(m) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
(n) Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(o) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(p) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(q) Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
(r) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Customer's details, the covers the Customer bought and any extensions.
(s) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(t) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
(d) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Accidental Damage
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(b) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(e) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

Article 4. Salvage
(a) When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

Article 5. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 6. Cancellation
(a) The Customer can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Customer can cancel at any time; the Provider will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Provider can cancel this policy by giving the Customer 30 days' written notice to the last address the Provider holds.

Article 7. Renewal
(a) The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 8. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 9. Electronic documents
(a) The Provider will send documents by email unless the Customer asks for paper copies.
(b) The Customer must tell the Provider if the Customer's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 10. Change of address
(a) The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
(b) The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 11. Complaints
(a) If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 12. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Provider will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 13. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Customer pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 14. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(a) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

Article 15. Assignment
(a) The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

Article 16. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 17. Interest
(a) The Provider will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 18. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 19. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 20. Transferring the plan
(a) The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
(b) The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

Article 21. Repair process
(a) After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
(b) The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

Article 22. Unrecoverable devices
(a) If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
(b) The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

Article 23. Premium payment
(a) The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 24. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Provider may check the details the Customer gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Provider may contact previous insurers to confirm the Customer's claims history.

Article 25. Sanctions
(a) The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 26. Claims documents
(a) The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
(b) The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 27. General exclusions

(b) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.
(d) The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.
(e) The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(f) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 28. Replacement devices

(b) Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
(c) Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

Article 29. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

(b) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 31. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Provider pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Provider may ask the Customer to repay the amount.

Article 32. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
