ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 1

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.4. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.5. Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.6. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.7. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.8. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
1.9. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.10. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.11. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.12. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
2.4. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

3. Breakdown
3.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
3.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

4. Communication
4.1. We will communicate with you in English.
4.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

5. Cooperation
5.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
5.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

6. Transferring the plan
6.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
6.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

7. Assignment
7.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

8. Governing law
8.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
8.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

9. Data protection
9.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
9.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
9.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

10. Interpretation
10.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
10.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
10.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

11. Instalment agreements
11.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
11.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

12. Waiver
12.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

13. Accidental Damage
13.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
13.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
13.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
13.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
13.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

14. Repair process
14.1. After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
14.2. We aim to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

15. Inflation
15.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
15.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

16. Data and backups
16.1. We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
16.2. You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

17. Taxes
17.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
17.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

18. Change of address
18.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
18.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

19. Exchange of information
19.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
19.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

20. Market conditions
20.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

21. Software support
21.1. Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
21.2. Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

22. Claims documents
22.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
22.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

23. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
23.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

24. Geographical limits
24.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
24.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

25. Automatic renewal
25.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
25.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

26. Cancellation
26.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
26.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
26.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

27. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
27.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
27.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
27.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
27.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
27.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

28. Severability
28.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

29. Subrogation
29.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
29.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

30. Accessibility
30.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

31. Renewal
31.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
31.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

32. Records and evidence
32.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
32.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
32.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

33. Electronic documents
33.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
33.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
33.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

34. Payment of claims
34.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
34.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

35. Notices
35.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
35.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

36. Third-party administrators
36.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
36.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

37. General exclusions
37.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
37.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
37.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
37.4. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
37.5. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

38. Making a claim
38.1. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
38.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
38.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

39. Duty of fair presentation
39.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
39.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
39.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

40. Changes in circumstances
40.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
40.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

41. Interest
41.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

42. How to read this document
42.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
42.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
42.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

43. Arbitration
43.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
43.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

44. Replacement devices
44.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
44.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
44.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

45. Unrecoverable devices
45.1. If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
45.2. We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

46. Discounts
46.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
46.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

47. Recovery of costs
47.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

48. Compensation scheme
48.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
48.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

49. Customer support
49.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
49.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

50. Reasonable precautions
50.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
50.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

51. Complaints
51.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
51.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
51.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

52. Sanctions
52.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

53. Fraud
53.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
53.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

54. Joint policyholders
54.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
54.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

55. Currency
55.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
55.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

56. Environmental commitment
56.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
56.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

57. Salvage
57.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
57.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

58. Premium payment
58.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
58.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

59. Other insurance
59.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
59.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.3 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.4 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
1.5 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.6 Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
1.7 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.8 Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
3.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 4 - OPTIONAL COVER: TRAVEL DELAY
4.1 We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
4.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3 We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
5.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
5.3 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.2 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 7 - WAIVER
7.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 8 - GOVERNING LAW
8.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
8.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 9 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
9.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
9.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 10 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
10.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
10.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 11 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
11.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
11.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
11.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 12 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
12.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
12.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 13 - CANCELLATION
13.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
13.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
13.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 14 - RENTAL CAR EXCESS
14.1 If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
14.2 This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

SECTION 15 - ASSIGNMENT
15.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 16 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
16.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
16.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 17 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
17.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

SECTION 18 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
18.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
18.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 19 - MARKET CONDITIONS
19.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 20 - SALVAGE
20.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
20.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 21 - ARBITRATION

22.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(e) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(f) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(g) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(h) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(i) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(j) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(k) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(l) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(m) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(n) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(o) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(p) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(q) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(r) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 5. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.

Article 6. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(f) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(g) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(h) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(i) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(j) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(k) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(l) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(m) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(n) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(o) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 4. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 5. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 6. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 10. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 11. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 12. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 13. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 14. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 15. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 16. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 17. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 18. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 19. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 20. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 21. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 22. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 23. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 24. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 25. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 26. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 27. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 28. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 29. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 30. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 31. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 32. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 33. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 34. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 35. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 36. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 37. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 38. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 39. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.3. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.4. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.5. Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.6. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.8. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.9. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.10. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.11. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.12. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.15. Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.16. Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.17. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5. The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Therapy Services
3.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
3.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
3.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
3.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

4. Vision Care
4.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
4.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
4.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
4.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

5. Dental Care
5.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
5.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
5.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
5.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
5.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
5.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

6. Optional cover: Hearing Care
6.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
6.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
6.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.5. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

8. Making a claim
8.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

9.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

10.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
10.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
10.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.

12.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
12.3. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

state.claim: File note. Yusuf Delgado (policy T156984, start date 26 October 2025) claims under Travel Delay for meals and taxis during a long airport delay. The schedule shows these covers: Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation; extensions: none. The incident happened on 23 June 2026 and was notified on 19 September 2026. The departure was delayed by 7 hours. The delay was caused by a technical fault with the aircraft. The return flight was scheduled for the following week. The trip was booked through an online travel agent. The assessed loss is $615.99.
state.policy:
TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(d) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(e) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(f) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(g) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(h) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(i) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(j) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(k) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
(l) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(m) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(n) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(o) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(p) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(q) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(r) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 6. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

Article 7. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

Article 8. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 9. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 10. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 11. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 12. Cancellation
(a) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 13. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 14. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 15. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 16. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 17. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 18. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 19. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 20. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 21. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 22. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 23. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 24. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 25. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 26. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 27. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 28. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 29. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 30. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 31. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 32. Legal expenses abroad
(a) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(b) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

Article 33. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.4. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.5. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.6. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
1.7. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.8. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.9. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.10. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.11. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.12. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.13. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
2.4. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

3. Accidental Damage
3.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
3.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
3.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
3.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

4.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

5. Breakdown
5.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
5.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
5.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
5.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
6.3. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.4. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

7.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
7.3. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

8.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

9. Claims documents

10. Complaints

14. Discounts

RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Oakfield Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Oakfield Assurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(c) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(d) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(e) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(f) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(g) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(h) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(i) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(j) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(k) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(l) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(m) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 6. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 10. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 11. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 12. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 13. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 14. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 15. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 16. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 17. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 18. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 19. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 20. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 21. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 22. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 23. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 24. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 25. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 26. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 27. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 28. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 29. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 30. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 31. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 32. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 33. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 34. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 35. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 36. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 37. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 38. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 39. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 40. Locks and keys
(a) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

Article 41. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 42. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 43. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 44. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 45. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 46. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 47. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

+from nose.tools import *  # noqa
 
+from api.base import utils as api_utils
+
+from tests.base import ApiTestCase
+
+class DummyAttrAttr(object):
+
+    def __init__(self, key):
+        self.key = key
+
+
+class DummyAttr(object):
+
+    def __init__(self, key):
+        self.key = key
+        self.attr_attr = DummyAttrAttr(key.upper())
+
+
+class Dummy(object):
+
+    def __init__(self, key):
+        self.attr = DummyAttr(key)
+        self.hash = {
+            'bang': DummyAttr(key)
+        }
+
+
+class APIUtilsTestCase(ApiTestCase):
+
+    def setUp(self):
+
+        self.dummy = Dummy('foo')
+        self.data = {
+            'foo': {
+                'bar': 'baz'
+            }
+        }
+
+    def test_deep_get_object(self):
+
+        attr = api_utils.deep_get(self.dummy, 'attr')
+        assert_true(isinstance(attr, DummyAttr))
+        assert_equal(attr.key, 'foo')
+
+    def test_deep_get_object_multiple_depth(self):
+
+        attr_attr = api_utils.deep_get(self.dummy, 'attr.attr_attr')
+        assert_true(isinstance(attr_attr, DummyAttrAttr))
+        assert_equal(attr_attr.key, 'FOO')
+
+    def test_deep_get_dict(self):
+
+        foo = api_utils.deep_get(self.data, 'foo')
+        assert_true(isinstance(foo, dict))
+        assert_equal(foo, {
+            'bar': 'baz'
+        })
+
+    def test_deep_get_dict_multiple_depth(self):
+
+        bar = api_utils.deep_get(self.data, 'foo.bar')
+        assert_true(isinstance(bar, str))
+        assert_equal(bar, 'baz')
+
+    def test_deep_get_object_and_dict(self):
+
+        hash_bang_attr = api_utils.deep_get(self.dummy, 'hash.bang.attr_attr')
+        assert_true(isinstance(hash_bang_attr, DummyAttrAttr))
+        assert_equal(hash_bang_attr.key, 'FOO')
+
+    def test_deep_get_key_not_found(self):
+
+        hash_bang_attr = api_utils.deep_get(self.dummy, 'hash.bang.baz')
+        assert_equal(hash_bang_attr, None)
+
+    def test_soft_get_object(self):
+
+        attr = api_utils.soft_get(self.dummy, 'attr')
+        assert_equal(attr.key, 'foo')
+
+    def test_soft_get_object_not_found(self):
+
+        bat = api_utils.soft_get(self.dummy, 'bat')
+        assert_equal(bat, None)
+
+    def test_soft_get_dict(self):
+
+        foo = api_utils.soft_get(self.data, 'foo')
+        assert_equal(foo, {
+            'bar': 'baz'
+        })
