GADGET COVER: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
I.2  Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
I.3  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.4  Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
I.5  Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
I.6  Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
I.7  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
I.8  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
I.9  Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.10  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.11  Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
I.12  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Customer's details, the covers the Customer bought and any extensions.
I.13  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Breakdown
III.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
III.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
III.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART IV: Accidental Damage
IV.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
IV.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IV.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
IV.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
IV.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART V: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
V.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
V.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
V.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
V.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.
VI.2  The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
VI.3  The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.4  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.5  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.6  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.3  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART VIII: Unrecoverable devices
VIII.1  If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
VIII.2  The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

PART IX: Taxes
IX.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
IX.2  If the tax rate changes, the Provider may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART X: Subrogation
X.1  The Provider will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Customer's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
X.2  The Provider can take action in the Customer's name to recover any payment the Provider makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XI: Assignment
XI.1  The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

XXI.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.

XXII.1  If the Provider does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Provider has given up the right to enforce it later.

XXIII.1  The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
XXIII.2  The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

XXIV.1  Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.

XXV.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XXV.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XXV.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

XXVI.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.

XXVII.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.

51.6. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

52.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

53. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)

A pipe under the kitchen sink burst suddenly during a cold night and soaked the flooring and furniture. The building is a converted warehouse with six flats. The assessed loss is $33,118.
state.policy:
HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(f) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(g) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(h) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(i) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(j) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(k) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(l) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(m) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(n) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(o) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(p) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(q) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(r) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(s) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(t) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(u) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 4. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 5. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 6. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 7. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 8. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 9. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 10. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 11. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 12. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 13. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 14. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 15. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 16. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 17. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 18. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 19. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 20. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 21. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 22. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 23. Locks and keys
(a) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

Article 24. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 25. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 26. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 27. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 28. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 29. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 30. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 31. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 32. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 33. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 34. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 35. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 36. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 37. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 38. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 39. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 40. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 41. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 42. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 43. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 44. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 45. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 46. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 47. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 48. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 49. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 50. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 51. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 52. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 53. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 54. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 55. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 56. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 57. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 58. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 59. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 60. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

CASE PRESENTATION A
HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2 Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.3 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.4 Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.5 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
3.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
3.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 4 - FLOOD
4.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 5 - ESCAPE OF WATER
5.1 We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
5.2 The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
5.3 We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
5.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

SECTION 6 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
6.1 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

SECTION 7 - MAKING A CLAIM
7.1 You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
7.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
7.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 8 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
8.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
8.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 9 - GOVERNING LAW

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.

I.6  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.7  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.8  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.9  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.10  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.11  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.12  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.

IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.

V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART VI: Escape of Water
VI.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.

VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.4. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.5. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.6. Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
1.7. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.8. Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.9. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.10. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.11. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.12. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.15. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.16. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.17. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.18. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.19. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.4. The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Breakdown
3.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
3.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
4.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
4.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

5. Accidental Damage
5.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
5.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
5.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
5.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.2. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
6.4. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
6.5. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

7. Making a claim
7.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
7.2. You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
7.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

8. Claims documents
8.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
8.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

9. Reasonable precautions
9.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
9.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

10. Third-party administrators
10.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
10.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

11. Customer support
11.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
11.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

12. Complaints
12.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
12.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
12.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

13. Instalment agreements
13.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
13.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

14. Inflation
14.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
14.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

15. Payment of claims
15.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
15.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

16. Data protection
16.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
16.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
16.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

17. Records and evidence
17.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
17.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
17.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

18. Duty of fair presentation
18.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
18.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
18.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

19. Automatic renewal
19.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
19.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

20. Discounts
20.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
20.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

21. Changes in circumstances
21.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
21.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

22. Subrogation
22.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
22.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

23. Replacement devices
23.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
23.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
23.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

24. Interest
24.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

25. Interpretation
25.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
25.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
25.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

26. Premium payment
26.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
26.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

27. Sanctions
27.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

28. Accessibility
28.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

29. Governing law
29.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
29.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

30. Taxes
30.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
30.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

31. Currency
31.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
31.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

- **6.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

- **10.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

- **11.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **11.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.3  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.4  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Flood
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VIII: Taxes
VIII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
VIII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART IX: Discounts
IX.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
IX.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART X: Currency
X.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
X.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XI: Exchange of information
XI.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
XI.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

PART XII: Cancellation
XII.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XII.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
XII.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XIII: Data protection
XIII.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIII.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIII.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XIV: Complaints
XIV.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XIV.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XIV.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XV: Duty of fair presentation
XV.1  The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
XV.2  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XV.3  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XVI: Reasonable precautions
XVI.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XVI.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XVII: Market conditions
XVII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XVIII: Claims documents
XVIII.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XVIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XIX: Contents temporarily removed
XIX.1  The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
XIX.2  Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

PART XX: Alternative accommodation
XX.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
XX.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
XX.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART XXI: Payment of claims
XXI.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XXI.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XXII: Interpretation
XXII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXII.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXII.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXIII: Communication
XXIII.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXIV: Subrogation
XXIV.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXIV.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXV: Salvage
XXV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XXV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.4** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Instalment agreements
- **3.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **3.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 4. Renewal
- **4.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **4.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 5. Reasonable precautions
- **5.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **5.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 6. Communication
- **6.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **6.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 7. Currency
- **7.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **7.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 8. Environmental commitment
- **8.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **8.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 9. Interpretation
- **9.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **9.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **9.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 10. Assignment
- **10.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 11. Breakdown
- **11.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **11.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **11.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **11.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **11.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 12. Interest
- **12.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 13. Market conditions
- **13.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 14. Governing law
- **14.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **14.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 15. Fraud
- **15.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **15.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 16. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **16.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **16.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **16.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **16.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **16.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 17. Complaints
- **17.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **17.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **17.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 18. Exchange of information
- **18.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **18.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 19. General exclusions
- **19.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **19.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **19.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 20. Transferring the plan
- **20.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **20.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 21. Software support
- **21.1** Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
- **21.2** Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

## 22. Premium payment
- **22.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **22.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 23. Cancellation
- **23.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **23.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
- **23.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 24. Making a claim
- **24.1** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **24.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **24.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

=== CLAIM ===
From: Kwame Horvat
Subject: Claim on policy B911174

Hello,

I would like to claim under Theft and Loss for a pair of earbuds. My policy started on August 22, 2026 and my schedule lists Accidental Damage, Breakdown, Theft and Loss (extensions: none). The incident happened on October 9, 2026. Kwame reported the theft to the police the same day. The earbuds were taken from Kwame's bag on a crowded train. The retailer's receipt was uploaded with the claim. The device is registered in Kwame's name.

I am sending this on October 20, 2026, which is when I first notified you. Your adjuster assessed the loss at $280.

Thanks,
Kwame

CASE PRESENTATION B
HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3 Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.4 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.5 Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.6 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.7 Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.8 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.9 High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.10 Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.11 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.12 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.13 Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.14 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.15 Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.16 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.17 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.18 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.19 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.20 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.21 Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - THEFT
3.1 We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
3.2 The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
3.5 We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
3.6 We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

SECTION 4 - FLOOD
4.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 5 - ESCAPE OF WATER
5.1 We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
5.2 The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
5.3 We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
5.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

SECTION 6 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
6.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
6.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
6.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
6.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.3 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.4 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.5 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 9 - TENANT'S IMPROVEMENTS
9.1 If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
9.2 This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

SECTION 10 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
10.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
10.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
10.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 11 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
11.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
11.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 12 - ACCESSIBILITY
12.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 13 - RENEWAL
13.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
13.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 14 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
14.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
14.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 15 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
15.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
15.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 16 - ASSIGNMENT
16.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 17 - COMMUNICATION
17.1 We will communicate with you in English.
17.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 18 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
18.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
18.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 19 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
19.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
19.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 20 - COMPLAINTS
20.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
20.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
20.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 21 - FRAUD
21.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
21.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 22 - SANCTIONS
22.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 23 - DISCOUNTS
23.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
23.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 24 - INTEREST
24.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 25 - CURRENCY
25.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
25.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 26 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
26.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
26.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
26.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 27 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
27.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
27.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 28 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
28.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
28.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 29 - CONTENTS TEMPORARILY REMOVED
29.1 Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
29.2 Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

SECTION 30 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
30.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
30.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
30.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 31 - SUBROGATION
31.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
31.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 32 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
32.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
32.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 33 - SEVERABILITY
33.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 34 - MARKET CONDITIONS
34.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 35 - SALVAGE
35.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
35.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 36 - CANCELLATION
36.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
36.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
36.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 37 - WAIVER
37.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 38 - ARBITRATION
38.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
38.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 39 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
39.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
39.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 1

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
