1.9. High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.10. Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.11. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.12. Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.15. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.19. Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Arbitration
3.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
3.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

4. Interpretation
4.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
4.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
4.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

5. Records and evidence
5.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
5.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
5.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

6. Tenant's improvements
6.1. If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
6.2. This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

7. Data protection
7.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
7.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
7.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

8. Environmental commitment
8.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
8.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

9. Locks and keys
9.1. If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
9.2. The most we will pay under this clause is $750 for any one claim.

10. Third-party administrators
10.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
10.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

11. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
11.1. We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
11.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
11.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
11.4. We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
11.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

12. Instalment agreements
12.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
12.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

13. Severability
13.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

14. Accessibility
14.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

15. Duty of fair presentation
15.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
15.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
15.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

16. Cancellation
16.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
16.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
16.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

17. Taxes
17.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
17.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

18. Notices
18.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
18.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

19. Freezer contents
19.1. We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
19.2. We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

20. Discounts
20.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
20.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

21. Assignment
21.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

22. Communication
22.1. We will communicate with you in English.
22.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

23. Claims documents
23.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
23.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

24. Alternative accommodation
24.1. If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
24.2. We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
24.3. Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

25. Payment of claims
25.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
25.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

26. Electronic documents
26.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
26.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
26.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

27. Reasonable precautions
27.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
27.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

28. Premium payment
28.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
28.2. If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

29. Geographical limits
29.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
29.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

30. Customer support
30.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
30.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

31. Subrogation
31.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
31.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

32. Salvage
32.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
32.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

33. Flood
33.1. We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
33.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
33.3. The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
33.4. We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

34. Fraud
34.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
34.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

35. Change of address
35.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
35.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

36. Cooperation
36.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
36.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

37. Governing law
37.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
37.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

38. Exchange of information
38.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
38.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

39. Garden and outdoor cover
39.1. We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
39.2. We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

40. Joint policyholders
40.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
40.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

41. How to read this document
41.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
41.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
41.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

42. Waiver
42.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

43. Complaints
43.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
43.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
43.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

44. Theft
44.1. We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
44.2. The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
44.3. The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
44.4. We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
44.5. We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
44.6. We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

45. Contents temporarily removed
45.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
45.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

46. Interest
46.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

47. Escape of Water
47.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
47.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
47.3. We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
47.4. We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

48. Sanctions
48.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

49. Compensation scheme
49.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
49.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

50. Automatic renewal
50.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
50.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

51. General exclusions
51.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
51.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
51.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
51.4. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
51.5. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
51.6. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

52. Renewal
52.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
52.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

53. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
53.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

54. Other insurance
54.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
54.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

55. Changes in circumstances
55.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
55.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

56. Recovery of costs
56.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

57. Market conditions
57.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

58. Making a claim
58.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
58.2. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
58.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

59. Inflation
59.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
59.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

60. Currency
60.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
60.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

1.13 Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.14 Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
1.15 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.16 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

1.20 Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
1.21 Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
1.22 Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: TRAVEL DELAY
3.1 We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

SECTION 4 - TRIP CANCELLATION
4.1 We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
4.5 We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

SECTION 5 - BAGGAGE AND PERSONAL BELONGINGS
5.1 We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
5.2 The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
5.3 The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
5.5 We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
5.6 We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

SECTION 6 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
6.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
6.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
6.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
6.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
6.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
6.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.3 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.3 You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 9 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
9.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
9.2 If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 10 - MISSED DEPARTURE
10.1 We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
10.2 You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

SECTION 11 - SEVERABILITY
11.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 12 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
12.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
12.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 13 - MARKET CONDITIONS
13.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 14 - SUBROGATION
14.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
14.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 15 - REPATRIATION
15.1 If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
15.2 We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

SECTION 16 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
16.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
16.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 17 - LEGAL EXPENSES ABROAD
17.1 We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
17.2 We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

SECTION 18 - DATA PROTECTION
18.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
18.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
18.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 19 - DISCOUNTS
19.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
19.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 20 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
20.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 21 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
21.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
21.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 22 - CURRENCY
22.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
22.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 23 - OTHER INSURANCE
23.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
23.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 24 - ARBITRATION
24.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
24.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 25 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
25.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
25.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 26 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
26.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
26.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 27 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
27.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
27.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 28 - RENTAL CAR EXCESS
28.1 If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
28.2 This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

SECTION 29 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
29.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 30 - SALVAGE
30.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
30.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 31 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
31.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
31.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 32 - FRAUD
32.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
32.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 33 - ASSIGNMENT
33.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 34 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
34.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
34.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 35 - SANCTIONS
35.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 36 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
36.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
36.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
36.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 37 - CANCELLATION
37.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
37.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
37.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 38 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
38.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
38.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 39 - INFLATION
39.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
39.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 40 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
40.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
40.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 41 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
41.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
41.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 42 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
42.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
42.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 43 - COOPERATION
43.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
43.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 44 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
44.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
44.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
44.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 45 - NOTICES
45.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
45.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 46 - GOVERNING LAW
46.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
46.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 47 - COMPLAINTS
47.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
47.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
47.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 48 - TAXES
48.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
48.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 49 - COMMUNICATION
49.1 We will communicate with you in English.
49.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 50 - EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE
50.1 Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
50.2 You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
50.3 The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

51.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.

51.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Staff Welfare Fund and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(c) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(d) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 6. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 7. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

Article 8. Leaving the plan
(a) Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
(b) Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

Article 9. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
(b) If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 10. Claims documents
(a) The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
(b) The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 11. Compensation scheme
(a) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 12. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 13. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

Article 14. Third-party administrators
(a) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(b) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 15. Customer support
(a) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

Article 16. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 17. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2 Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.3 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.4 Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.5 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.6 Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.7 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.8 High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.9 Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.10 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.11 Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.12 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.13 Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - ESCAPE OF WATER
3.1 We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
3.2 The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
3.3 We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
3.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

SECTION 4 - FLOOD
4.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 5 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
5.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
5.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
5.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 6 - THEFT
6.1 We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
6.2 The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
6.3 The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
6.4 We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
6.5 We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
6.6 We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.3 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.4 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.5 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.6 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
9.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
9.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
9.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 10 - ALTERNATIVE ACCOMMODATION
10.1 If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
10.2 We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
10.3 Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

SECTION 11 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
11.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
11.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 12 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
12.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
12.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 13 - GOVERNING LAW
13.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
13.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 14 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
14.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
14.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 15 - MARKET CONDITIONS
15.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 16 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
16.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
16.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 17 - TENANT'S IMPROVEMENTS
17.1 If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
17.2 This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

SECTION 18 - INTERPRETATION
18.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
18.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
18.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 19 - INFLATION
19.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
19.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 20 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
20.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
20.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 21 - ARBITRATION
21.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
21.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 22 - RENEWAL
22.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
22.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 23 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
23.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 24 - SUBROGATION
24.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
24.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 25 - COMMUNICATION
25.1 We will communicate with you in English.
25.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 26 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
26.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
26.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 27 - SALVAGE
27.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
27.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 28 - OTHER INSURANCE
28.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
28.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 29 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
29.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
29.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 30 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
30.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
30.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 31 - NOTICES
31.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
31.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 32 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
32.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
32.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 33 - DISCOUNTS
33.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
33.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 34 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
34.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
34.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 35 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
35.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
35.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 36 - SANCTIONS
36.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 37 - CURRENCY
37.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
37.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 38 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
38.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
38.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 39 - DATA PROTECTION
39.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
39.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
39.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 40 - COOPERATION
40.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
40.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 41 - ASSIGNMENT
41.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 42 - ACCESSIBILITY
42.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 43 - INTEREST
43.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 44 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
44.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
44.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
44.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 45 - COMPLAINTS
45.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
45.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
45.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 46 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
46.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 47 - WAIVER
47.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 48 - LOCKS AND KEYS
48.1 If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
48.2 The most we will pay under this clause is $750 for any one claim.

SECTION 49 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
49.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
49.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 50 - GARDEN AND OUTDOOR COVER
50.1 We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
50.2 We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

SECTION 51 - SEVERABILITY
51.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 52 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
52.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
52.2 If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 53 - FRAUD
53.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
53.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 54 - CANCELLATION
54.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
54.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
54.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 55 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
55.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
55.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
55.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 56 - CONTENTS TEMPORARILY REMOVED
56.1 Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
56.2 Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

SECTION 57 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
57.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
57.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
57.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 58 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
58.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
58.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 59 - TAXES
59.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
59.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 60 - FREEZER CONTENTS
60.1 We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.

Issued by Lantern General Insurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.6  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.7  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.8  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.9  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.10  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.11  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.12  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.13  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.14  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.15  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.16  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.17  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.18  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART VI: Escape of Water
VI.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.2  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.3  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

IX.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.

state.policy:
SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(d) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(e) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(f) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
(g) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(h) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(i) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(j) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(k) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
(l) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
(m) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(n) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(o) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(p) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(q) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Change of address
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 4. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
(b) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 5. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 6. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 7. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 8. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 9. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 10. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 11. Assignment
(a) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 12. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 13. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 14. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 15. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 16. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 17. Premium payment
(a) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 18. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 19. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 20. Repatriation
(a) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(b) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

Article 21. Personal liability
(a) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(b) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

Article 22. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 23. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 24. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 25. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 26. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 27. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 28. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 29. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 30. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 31. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

Article 32. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 33. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 34. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 35. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 36. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 37. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 38. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 39. Cooperation
(a) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

GADGET COVER: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Issued by Circuit Care Services
In this policy, "the Provider" means Circuit Care Services and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
(b) Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
(c) Limit means the most the Provider will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(d) Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.

Article 2. Limits and service fee
(a) Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(b) Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
(c) Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(d) The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(a) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 6. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Provider may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 7. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 8. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Customer must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Customer must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 9. Payment of claims
(a) The Provider will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Customer's name.
(b) The Provider aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Provider needs.

Article 10. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
(b) If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Customer gives incorrect information carelessly, the Provider may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 11. Cancellation
(a) The Customer can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Customer can cancel at any time; the Provider will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Provider can cancel this policy by giving the Customer 30 days' written notice to the last address the Provider holds.

Article 12. Inflation
(a) The Provider may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Customer's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 13. Replacement devices

(c) Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

Article 14. Sanctions

Article 17. Geographical limits

(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 18. Severability

Article 19. Assignment

Article 20. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

- **1.11** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
