- **1.13** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.14** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
- **1.17** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.18** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.19** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Breakdown
- **3.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **3.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 4. Accidental Damage
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **4.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 5. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **5.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **5.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **6.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.2** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 8. Data protection
- **8.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **8.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **8.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 9. Salvage
- **9.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **9.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 10. Interest
- **10.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 11. How to read this document
- **11.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **11.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **11.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 12. Payment of claims
- **12.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **12.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 13. Other insurance
- **13.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **13.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 14. Governing law
- **14.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **14.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 15. Fraud
- **15.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **15.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 16. Inflation
- **16.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **16.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 17. Sanctions
- **17.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 18. Environmental commitment
- **18.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **18.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 19. Arbitration
- **19.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **19.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 20. Currency
- **20.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **20.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 21. Complaints
- **21.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **21.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **21.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 22. Discounts
- **22.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **22.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 23. Subrogation
- **23.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **23.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 24. Accessibility
- **24.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 25. Customer support
- **25.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **25.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 26. Unrecoverable devices
- **26.1** If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
- **26.2** We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

## 27. Joint policyholders
- **27.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **27.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 28. Premium payment
- **28.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **28.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 29. Exchange of information
- **29.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **29.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 30. Duty of fair presentation
- **30.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **30.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **30.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 31. Transferring the plan
- **31.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **31.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 32. Severability
- **32.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 33. Electronic documents
- **33.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **33.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **33.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 34. Geographical limits
- **34.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **34.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 35. Communication
- **35.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **35.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 36. Cooperation
- **36.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **36.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 37. Renewal
- **37.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **37.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 38. Interpretation
- **38.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **38.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **38.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 39. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **39.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 40. Cancellation
- **40.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **40.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
- **40.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 41. Third-party administrators
- **41.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **41.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 42. Claims documents
- **42.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **42.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 43. Compensation scheme
- **43.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **43.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 44. Change of address
- **44.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **44.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 45. Replacement devices
- **45.1** If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
- **45.2** Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
- **45.3** Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

## 46. Reasonable precautions
- **46.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **46.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 47. Notices
- **47.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **47.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 48. Data and backups
- **48.1** We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
- **48.2** You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

## 49. Recovery of costs
- **49.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 50. Instalment agreements
- **50.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **50.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

- **51.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **51.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

(d) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

(f) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

+        :type nums1: List[int]
+        :type nums2: List[int]
+        :rtype: float

+        if m > n:
+            nums1, nums2, m, n = nums2, nums1, n, m
+        if n == 0:

+        iMin, iMax, half = 0, m, (m + n + 1) / 2
+        while iMin <= iMax:

+            j = half - i

+            elif i > 0 and j < n and nums1[i-1] > nums2[j]:

state.policy:
EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.4  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.5  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.6  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.7  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.8  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.17  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Hearing Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART IV: Therapy Services
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART V: Vision Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART VI: Dental Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
VI.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
VI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
VI.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
VI.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
VI.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART IX: Geographical limits
IX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
IX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART X: Reasonable precautions
X.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
X.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XI: Environmental commitment
XI.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XI.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XII: Severability
XII.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XIII: Customer support
XIII.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XIII.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART XIV: Payment of claims
XIV.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
XIV.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XV: Interpretation
XV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XVI: Automatic renewal
XVI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XVI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XVII: Waiver
XVII.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVIII: Notices
XVIII.1  Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
XVIII.2  Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XIX: Premium payment
XIX.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XIX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XX: Accessibility
XX.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXI: Joint policyholders
XXI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XXI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XXII: Cooperation
XXII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XXIII: Recovery of costs
XXIII.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXIV: Records and evidence
XXIV.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXIV.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXIV.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXV: Data protection
XXV.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXV.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXV.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART XXVI: Appeals
XXVI.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
XXVI.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
XXVI.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART XXVII: Other insurance
XXVII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
XXVII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

PART XXVIII: Currency
XXVIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXVIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXIX: Sanctions
XXIX.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXX: Change of address
XXX.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXX.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXXI: Taxes
XXXI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XXXI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXXII: Fraud
XXXII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXII.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIII: Claims documents
XXXIII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXXIII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIV: Exchange of information
XXXIV.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XXXIV.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART XXXV: Salvage
XXXV.1  When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
XXXV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

PART XXXVI: Duty of fair presentation
XXXVI.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XXXVI.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXXVI.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXXVII: Communication
XXXVII.1  The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
XXXVII.2  The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXXVIII: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXXVIII.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXXIX: Inflation
XXXIX.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXIX.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXX: How to read this document
XXXX.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XXXX.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XXXX.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XXXXI: Instalment agreements
XXXXI.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXXXI.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXXXII: Coordination of benefits
XXXXII.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
XXXXII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART XXXXIII: Wellness allowance
XXXXIII.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXXXIII.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(e) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(f) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(g) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(h) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(i) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(j) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
(k) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(l) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(m) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(n) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(o) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 5. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 6. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

Article 10. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 11. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 12. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 13. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 14. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 15. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 16. Change of address
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 17. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 18. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 19. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

state.policy:
DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
I.2  Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
I.3  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Provider, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.4  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.5  Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
I.6  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.7  Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
I.8  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.9  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
I.10  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
I.11  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.12  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.13  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
II.4  The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Sanctions
III.1  The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART IV: Unrecoverable devices
IV.1  If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
IV.2  The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

PART V: Interpretation
V.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
V.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
V.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART VI: Third-party administrators
VI.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
VI.2  Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART VII: Communication
VII.1  The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
VII.2  The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART VIII: How to read this document
VIII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
VIII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
VIII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART IX: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
IX.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
IX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
IX.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IX.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
IX.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART X: Records and evidence
X.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
X.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
X.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XI: Accidental Damage
XI.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
XI.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
XI.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
XI.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
XI.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART XII: Change of address
XII.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
XII.2  The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XIII: Breakdown
XIII.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
XIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XIII.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
XIII.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
XIII.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART XIV: Changes in circumstances
XIV.1  The Customer must tell the Provider as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XIV.2  The Provider may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XV: Compensation scheme
XV.1  The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XV.2  If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XVI: General exclusions
XVI.1  The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XVI.2  The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XVI.3  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
XVI.4  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

PART XVII: Making a claim
XVII.1  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XVII.2  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XVII.3  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART XVIII: Claims documents
XVIII.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
XVIII.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XIX: Data protection
XIX.1  The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIX.2  The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIX.3  The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

PART XX: Premium payment
XX.1  The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXI: Cancellation
XXI.1  The Customer can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XXI.2  After the first 14 days the Customer can cancel at any time; the Provider will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
XXI.3  The Provider can cancel this policy by giving the Customer 30 days' written notice to the last address the Provider holds.

PART XXII: Environmental commitment
XXII.1  Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXII.2  The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXIII: Replacement devices
XXIII.1  If the Provider cannot repair the Customer's device economically, the Provider will replace it with a replacement device.
XXIII.2  Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
XXIII.3  Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

CASE PRESENTATION A
HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3 Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.4 Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.5 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.6 High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.7 Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.8 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.9 Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.10 Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.11 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.12 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.13 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.14 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.15 Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - ESCAPE OF WATER
3.1 We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
3.2 The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
3.3 We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
3.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

SECTION 4 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
4.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
4.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
4.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 5 - FLOOD
5.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
5.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
5.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 6 - THEFT
6.1 We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
6.2 The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
6.3 The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
6.4 We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
6.5 We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
6.6 We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
9.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
9.2 If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 10 - DISCOUNTS
10.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
10.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 11 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
11.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
11.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
11.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 12 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
12.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
12.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 13 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
13.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
13.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 14 - WAIVER
14.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 15 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
15.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
15.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 16 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
16.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
16.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
16.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 17 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
17.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 18 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
18.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
18.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 19 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
19.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
19.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 20 - INTERPRETATION
20.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
20.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
20.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 21 - SANCTIONS
21.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 22 - MARKET CONDITIONS
22.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 23 - CANCELLATION
23.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
23.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
23.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 24 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
24.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
24.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 25 - SEVERABILITY
25.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 26 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
26.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
26.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 27 - TAXES
27.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
27.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 28 - RENEWAL
28.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
28.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 29 - ASSIGNMENT
29.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 30 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
30.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
30.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 31 - GARDEN AND OUTDOOR COVER
31.1 We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
31.2 We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

SECTION 32 - CURRENCY
32.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
32.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 33 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
33.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
33.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 34 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
34.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
34.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 35 - FREEZER CONTENTS
35.1 We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
35.2 We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

SECTION 36 - NOTICES
36.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
36.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 37 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
37.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
37.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 38 - GOVERNING LAW
38.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
38.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 39 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
39.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
39.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 40 - COMMUNICATION
40.1 We will communicate with you in English.
40.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 41 - CONTENTS TEMPORARILY REMOVED
41.1 Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
41.2 Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.3** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.4** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.7** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.8** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.9** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.12** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.15** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.16** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Flood
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 4. Escape of Water
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **4.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **4.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Theft
- **6.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **6.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **6.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.5** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 9. Cancellation
- **9.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **9.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
- **9.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 10. Assignment
- **10.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 11. Electronic documents
- **11.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **11.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **11.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 12. Fraud
- **12.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **12.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 13. Accessibility
- **13.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 14. Joint policyholders
- **14.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **14.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 15. Locks and keys
- **15.1** If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
- **15.2** The most we will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

## 16. Third-party administrators
- **16.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **16.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 17. Renewal
- **17.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **17.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 18. Geographical limits
- **18.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **18.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 19. Tenant's improvements
- **19.1** If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
- **19.2** This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

## 20. Severability
- **20.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 21. Changes in circumstances
- **21.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **21.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 22. Sanctions
- **22.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 23. Arbitration
- **23.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **23.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 24. Notices
- **24.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **24.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 25. Inflation
- **25.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **25.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 26. Interpretation
- **26.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **26.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **26.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 27. Discounts
- **27.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **27.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 28. Customer support
- **28.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **28.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 29. Complaints
- **29.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **29.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **29.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 30. Cooperation
- **30.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **30.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 31. Alternative accommodation
- **31.1** If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
- **31.2** We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
- **31.3** Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

## 32. Garden and outdoor cover
- **32.1** We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
- **32.2** We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

## 33. Claims documents
- **33.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **33.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 34. Change of address
- **34.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **34.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 35. Other insurance
- **35.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **35.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 36. Governing law
- **36.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **36.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 37. Environmental commitment
- **37.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **37.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 38. Waiver
- **38.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 39. Records and evidence
- **39.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **39.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **39.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 40. Currency
- **40.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **40.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 41. Duty of fair presentation
- **41.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **41.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **41.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 42. Payment of claims
- **42.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **42.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 43. Instalment agreements
- **43.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **43.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 44. Communication
- **44.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **44.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 45. Exchange of information
- **45.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **45.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 46. Premium payment
- **46.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **46.2** If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 47. Freezer contents
- **47.1** We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
- **47.2** We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

## 48. Interest
- **48.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 49. Compensation scheme
- **49.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **49.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 50. Data protection
- **50.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **50.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **50.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 51. Market conditions
- **51.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 52. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **52.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 53. Subrogation
- **53.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **53.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.
