HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.6  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.7  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.8  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.9  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.10  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.11  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.12  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.13  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.14  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.18  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.19  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Changes in circumstances
V.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
V.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART VI: Geographical limits
VI.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
VI.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART VII: Instalment agreements
VII.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
VII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART VIII: Currency
VIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
VIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART IX: Cancellation
IX.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
IX.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
IX.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART X: Notices
X.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
X.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XI: Accessibility
XI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XII: Complaints
XII.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XII.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XII.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XIII: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
XIII.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
XIII.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
XIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
XIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
XIII.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART XIV: Recovery of costs
XIV.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XV: Interest
XV.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVI: Waiver
XVI.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVII: How to read this document
XVII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XVII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XVII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XVIII: Flood
XVIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
XVIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XVIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XVIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XIX: Freezer contents
XIX.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
XIX.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART XX: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)

# Gadget Cover: Terms and Conditions
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.4** Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
- **1.5** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.6** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.7** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.8** Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
- **1.9** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.12** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.13** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.14** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
- **1.17** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.18** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.19** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **3.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 4. Accidental Damage
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **4.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 5. Breakdown
- **5.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **5.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **6.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **6.4** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 8. Cooperation
- **8.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **8.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 9. Exchange of information
- **9.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **9.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 10. Accessibility
- **10.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 11. Market conditions
- **11.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 12. Fraud
- **12.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **12.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 13. Data protection
- **13.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **13.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **13.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 14. Unrecoverable devices
- **14.1** If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
- **14.2** We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

## 15. Currency
- **15.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **15.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 16. Renewal
- **16.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **16.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 17. Payment of claims
- **17.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **17.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 18. Claims documents
- **18.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **18.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 19. Instalment agreements
- **19.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **19.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 20. Recovery of costs
- **20.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 21. Reasonable precautions
- **21.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **21.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 22. Other insurance
- **22.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **22.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 23. Duty of fair presentation
- **23.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **23.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **23.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 24. Taxes
- **24.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **24.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 25. Communication
- **25.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **25.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 26. Geographical limits
- **26.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **26.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 27. Replacement devices
- **27.1** If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
- **27.2** Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
- **27.3** Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

## 28. Assignment
- **28.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 29. Customer support
- **29.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **29.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 30. Records and evidence
- **30.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **30.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **30.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 31. Interest
- **31.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 32. Software support
- **32.1** Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
- **32.2** Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

## 33. How to read this document
- **33.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **33.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **33.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 34. Cancellation
- **34.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **34.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
- **34.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 35. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **35.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 36. Waiver
- **36.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 37. Subrogation
- **37.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **37.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 38. Joint policyholders
- **38.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **38.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 39. Transferring the plan
- **39.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **39.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 40. Arbitration
- **40.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **40.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 41. Environmental commitment
- **41.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **41.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 42. Electronic documents
- **42.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **42.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **42.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 43. Sanctions
- **43.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 44. Compensation scheme
- **44.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **44.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 45. Automatic renewal
- **45.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **45.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 46. Discounts
- **46.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **46.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 47. Premium payment
- **47.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **47.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 48. Interpretation
- **48.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **48.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **48.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 49. Severability
- **49.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 50. Notices
- **50.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **50.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
I.2  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.3  Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
I.4  Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
I.5  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.6  Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
I.7  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.8  Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
I.9  Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.10  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
I.11  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
I.12  Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
I.13  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.14  Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Baggage and Personal Belongings
III.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART IV: Optional cover: Travel Delay
IV.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART V: Trip Cancellation
V.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART VI: Emergency Medical Expenses
VI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
VI.5  The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
VI.6  The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.2  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART IX: Currency

IX.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

X.2  The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XI: Joint policyholders
XI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

XII.1  The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
XII.2  This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
XII.3  The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

PART XIII: Market conditions
XIII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XIV: Electronic documents
XIV.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
XIV.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
XIV.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XV: Waiver
XV.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVI: Rental car excess
XVI.1  If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.

XVIII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XIX: Taxes

XIX.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XX: Legal expenses abroad
XX.1  The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
XX.2  The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

PART XXI: Inflation
XXI.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXI.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXII: Changes in circumstances
XXII.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXII.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XXIII: Claims documents
XXIII.1  The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIV: Discounts
XXIV.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXIV.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.2  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Change of address
III.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
III.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART IV: Other insurance
IV.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
IV.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

PART V: Duty of fair presentation
V.1  The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
V.2  If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
V.3  If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART VI: Joint policyholders
VI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
VI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART VII: Market conditions
VII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART VIII: Optional cover: Travel Delay
VIII.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
VIII.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
VIII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART IX: General exclusions
IX.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
IX.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
IX.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART X: Interpretation
X.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
X.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
X.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XI: Legal expenses abroad
XI.1  The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
XI.2  The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

PART XII: Records and evidence
XII.1  The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XII.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XIII: Exchange of information

XIII.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

PART XIV: Making a claim
XIV.1  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XIV.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XIV.3  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART XV: Cancellation

XV.2  After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XV.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XVI: Accessibility
XVI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XVII: Complaints
XVII.1  If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XVII.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XVII.3  If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XVIII: Notices

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.4** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.7** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.8** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.9** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.10** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.11** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
- **1.12** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.15** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.16** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.17** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.18** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.19** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.20** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
- **1.21** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **4.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **4.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 6. Trip Cancellation
- **6.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **6.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **6.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.4** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.5** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.2** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **8.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 9. Legal expenses abroad
- **9.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **9.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 10. Payment of claims
- **10.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **10.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 11. Duty of fair presentation
- **11.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **11.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **11.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 12. Subrogation
- **12.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **12.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 13. Taxes
- **13.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **13.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 14. Records and evidence
- **14.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **14.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **14.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 15. Currency
- **15.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **15.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 16. Assignment
- **16.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 17. Customer support
- **17.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **17.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 18. Compensation scheme
- **18.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **18.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 19. Severability
- **19.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 20. Environmental commitment
- **20.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **20.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 21. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **21.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 22. Exchange of information
- **22.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **22.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 23. Waiver
- **23.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 24. Third-party administrators
- **24.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **24.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 25. Recovery of costs
- **25.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 26. Arbitration
- **26.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **26.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 27. Emergency assistance
- **27.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **27.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **27.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 28. Market conditions
- **28.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 29. Discounts
- **29.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **29.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 30. Personal liability
- **30.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **30.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **30.3** The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 31. Interest
- **31.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 32. Automatic renewal
- **32.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **32.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 33. Governing law
- **33.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **33.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 34. Fraud
- **34.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **34.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 35. Sanctions
- **35.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 36. Accessibility
- **36.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 37. Changes in circumstances
- **37.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **37.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 38. Notices
- **38.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **38.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 39. Repatriation
- **39.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **39.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 40. Data protection
- **40.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **40.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **40.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 41. Joint policyholders
- **41.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **41.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 42. Salvage
- **42.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **42.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.

III.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
IV.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
V.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
V.3  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VI: Personal liability
VI.1  The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
VI.2  This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

PART VII: Customer support
VII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
VII.2  Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART VIII: Change of address
VIII.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
VIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART IX: Renewal

PART X: Taxes

PART XI: Exchange of information

XI.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

PART XII: Other insurance

XII.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

PART XIII: Fraud

XVI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
XVI.2  The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

PART XVII: Automatic renewal
XVII.1  Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XVII.2  The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XVIII: Rental car excess
XVIII.1  If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
XVIII.2  This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

PART XIX: Data protection
XIX.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIX.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIX.3  The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XX: Arbitration
XX.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.

XXIII.2  The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXIV: Reasonable precautions
XXIV.1  The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXIV.2  The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXV: Sanctions

--- a/tests/test_engines.py
+++ b/tests/test_engines.py
@@ -83 +83,103 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python
 
+from __future__ import print_function
+
+import unittest
+
+try:
+    from unittest import mock
+except ImportError:
+    import mock
+
+import imp
+import os.path
+
+
+import engines
+
+
+class TestInit(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_init(self):
+        mock_engines = {}
+
+        mock_listdir = mock.Mock(return_value=(
+                'text_engine.txt',
+                '0_engine.py',
+                '.period_engine.py',
+                '@at_engine.py',
+                '__init__.py',
+                '_underscore_engine.py',
+                'normal_engine.py',
+                'compiled_engine.pyc',
+                'optimized_engine.pyo',
+            ))
+
+        valid_engines = {
+                '_underscore_engine':   ('UnderscoreEngine', 'underscore'),
+                'normal_engine':        ('NormalEngine',     'normal'),
+                'compiled_engine':      ('CompiledEngine',   'compiled'),
+                'optimized_engine':     ('OptimizedEngine',  'optimized'),
+            }
+
+        result_dict = {handle: None for __, (__, handle) in valid_engines.items()}
+
+        def mock_import_module(name, package):
+            self.assertEqual(package, 'engines')
+
+            assert name.startswith('.')
+            name = name[1:]
+
+            module = imp.new_module('%s.%s' % (package, name))
+
+            if name == '__init__':
+                module.Engine = engines.Engine
+            else:
+                self.assertIn(name, valid_engines)
+                class_name, engine_handle = valid_engines[name]
+
+                class MockEngine(engines.Engine):
+                    handle = engine_handle
+
+                MockEngine.__name__ = class_name
+                MockEngine.__qualname__ = class_name
+
+                result_dict[engine_handle] = MockEngine
+                setattr(module, class_name, MockEngine)
+
+            return module
+
+        with mock.patch.object(engines, 'engines', mock_engines), \
+             mock.patch('os.listdir', mock_listdir), \
+             mock.patch('importlib.import_module', mock_import_module):
+            engines._init()
+
+        mock_listdir.assert_called_once_with(os.path.dirname(engines.__file__))
+        self.assertDictEqual(mock_engines, result_dict)
+
+
+class TestEngine(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_not_instantiable(self):
+        self.assertRaises(AssertionError, engines.Engine, dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+    def test_handle_is_none(self):
+        class TestEngine(engines.Engine):
+            pass
+
+        engine = TestEngine(dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+        self.assertIsNone(engine.handle)
+
+    def test_apply_not_implemented(self):
+        class TestEngine(engines.Engine):
+            pass
+
+        engine = TestEngine(dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+        self.assertRaises(NotImplementedError, engine.apply, {})
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()
+

24.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.

31.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.

32.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
32.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
32.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

33.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.

45.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.

46.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

47. Inflation
47.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
47.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

48. Taxes
48.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
48.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

49. Legal expenses abroad
49.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
49.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

50. Recovery of costs
50.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

51. Discounts
51.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
51.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

52. General exclusions
52.1. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
52.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
52.3. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

53. Assignment
53.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

54. Payment of claims
54.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
54.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

55. Arbitration
55.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
55.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

56. Cancellation
56.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
56.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
56.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

57. Making a claim
57.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
57.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
57.3. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

58. Currency
58.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
58.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

59. Reasonable precautions
59.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
59.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

60. Premium payment
60.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
60.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.3** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.4** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
- **1.7** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.8** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.9** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
- **1.12** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.13** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.14** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.17** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.18** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Flood
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Escape of Water
- **6.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **6.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.6** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

- **8.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.3** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

- **9.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.

- **16.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.

- **17.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

- **18.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.

Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
(d) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(e) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(f) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(g) Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(h) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(i) Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
(j) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(k) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(l) Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
(m) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(n) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(o) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(p) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(q) Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
(r) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Vision Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(d) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

Article 4. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 5. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.

XII.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.

PART XIII: Interest
XIII.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XIV: Escape of Water
