# Group Health Cash Plan
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.6** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.7** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.10** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.11** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.12** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.13** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.14** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.15** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.16** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.17** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.18** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.19** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.20** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.21** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Governing law
- **3.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **3.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 4. Claims documents
- **4.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **4.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 5. Dental Care
- **5.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **5.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **5.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **5.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 6. Waiver
- **6.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 7. Inflation
- **7.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **7.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 8. Notices
- **8.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **8.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 9. Duty of fair presentation
- **9.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **9.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **9.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 10. Premium payment
- **10.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **10.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 11. Joint policyholders
- **11.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **11.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 12. Taxes
- **12.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **12.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 13. Electronic documents
- **13.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **13.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **13.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 14. Vision Care
- **14.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **14.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **14.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **14.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 15. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **15.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **15.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **15.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **15.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 16. Subrogation
- **16.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **16.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 17. Complaints
- **17.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **17.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **17.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 18. Reasonable precautions
- **18.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **18.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 19. Payment of claims
- **19.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **19.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 20. Sanctions
- **20.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 21. Therapy Services
- **21.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **21.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **21.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **21.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 22. Cooperation
- **22.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **22.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 23. Dependants
- **23.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **23.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 24. General exclusions
- **24.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **24.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **24.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **24.4** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **24.5** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 25. Arbitration
- **25.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **25.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 26. Currency
- **26.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **26.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 27. Records and evidence
- **27.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **27.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **27.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 28. Geographical limits
- **28.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **28.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 29. Making a claim
- **29.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **29.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **29.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.3** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.4** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.5** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.6** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.7** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.8** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Escape of Water
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
- **4.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **4.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 5. Flood
- **5.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **6.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 8. Third-party administrators
- **8.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **8.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 9. Instalment agreements
- **9.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **9.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 10. Fraud
- **10.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **10.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 11. Market conditions
- **11.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 12. Freezer contents
- **12.1** We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
- **12.2** We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

## 13. Communication
- **13.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **13.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 14. Accessibility
- **14.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 15. Other insurance
- **15.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **15.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 16. Contents temporarily removed
- **16.1** Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
- **16.2** Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

## 17. Premium payment
- **17.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **17.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 18. Governing law
- **18.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **18.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 19. Records and evidence
- **19.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **19.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **19.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 20. Exchange of information
- **20.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **20.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 21. Inflation
- **21.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **21.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 22. Severability
- **22.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.

- **1.9** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.10** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.11** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.12** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.13** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.14** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.15** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.16** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.17** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.

- **6.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **6.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **6.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.

- **1.3** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.4** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.7** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.8** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.9** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.10** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.11** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.12** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.13** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.14** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.15** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.16** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.17** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. Taxes
- **4.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **4.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

- **5.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.

- **6.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.

- **7.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

- **8.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **8.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **8.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **8.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **8.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **8.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 9. Emergency assistance
- **9.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **9.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **9.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 10. Trip Cancellation
- **10.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **10.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **10.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **10.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **10.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 11. Rental car excess
- **11.1** If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
- **11.2** This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

## 12. Compensation scheme
- **12.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **12.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 13. Subrogation
- **13.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **13.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 14. Geographical limits
- **14.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **14.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 15. Sanctions
- **15.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 16. Fraud
- **16.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **16.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 17. Governing law
- **17.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **17.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 18. Instalment agreements
- **18.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **18.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 19. Assignment
- **19.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

- **20.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

- **21.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **21.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

- **22.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **22.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

- **23.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.

- **23.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.

- **24.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

- **28.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.

- **29.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

- **33.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.

- **4.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **4.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **5.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **5.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

- **6.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **6.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **6.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

- **8.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **8.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 9. Joint policyholders
- **9.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **9.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 10. Assignment
- **10.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 11. Changes in circumstances
- **11.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **11.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 12. Recovery of costs
- **12.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 13. Communication
- **13.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **13.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 14. Market conditions
- **14.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 15. Inflation
- **15.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **15.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 16. Taxes
- **16.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **16.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 17. Notices

- **17.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

- **18.1** If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
- **18.2** This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

- **19.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **19.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **19.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 20. Accessibility
- **20.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

- **21.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **21.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

- **22.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **22.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 23. How to read this document
- **23.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **23.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **23.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

- **24.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.

- **26.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.

- **27.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **27.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 28. Complaints
- **28.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **28.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **28.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 29. Compensation scheme
- **29.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **29.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 30. Fraud
- **30.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **30.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 31. Instalment agreements
- **31.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **31.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 32. Currency
- **32.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **32.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

- **33.1** We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
- **33.2** You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

## 34. Renewal
- **34.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **34.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 35. Geographical limits
- **35.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **35.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 36. Duty of fair presentation
- **36.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **36.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **36.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 37. Data protection
- **37.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **37.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **37.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 38. Exchange of information
- **38.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **38.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 39. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **39.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 40. Automatic renewal
- **40.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **40.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 41. Cooperation
- **41.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **41.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 42. Severability
- **42.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 43. Change of address
- **43.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **43.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 44. Sanctions
- **44.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 45. Premium payment
- **45.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **45.2** If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 46. Third-party administrators
- **46.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **46.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 47. Repatriation
- **47.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **47.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 48. Emergency assistance
- **48.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **48.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **48.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 49. Personal liability
- **49.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **49.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **49.3** The most we will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 50. Subrogation
- **50.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **50.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 51. Records and evidence
- **51.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **51.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **51.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 52. Legal expenses abroad
- **52.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **52.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 53. Claims documents
- **53.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **53.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 54. Reasonable precautions
- **54.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **54.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 55. Arbitration
- **55.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **55.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 56. Discounts
- **56.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **56.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 57. Interest
- **57.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 58. Waiver
- **58.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 59. Other insurance
- **59.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **59.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 60. Environmental commitment
- **60.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **60.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Trip Cancellation
3.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
3.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

4. General exclusions
4.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
4.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

5. Making a claim
5.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
5.2. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
5.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

6. Assignment
6.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

7. Arbitration
7.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
7.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

8. Electronic documents
8.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
8.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
8.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

9. Data protection
9.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
9.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
9.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

10. Payment of claims
10.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
10.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

11. Duty of fair presentation
11.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
11.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
11.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

12. Personal liability
12.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
12.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
12.3. The most we will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

14. Taxes

15. Accessibility
15.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

16. Premium payment
16.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
16.2. If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

17. Waiver
17.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

18. Fraud
18.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
18.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

19.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
19.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
19.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

20. Recovery of costs
20.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

21. Cooperation
21.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
21.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

22. Cancellation
22.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
22.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
22.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

23. Legal expenses abroad
23.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
23.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

24. Geographical limits
24.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
24.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

25. Subrogation
25.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
25.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

26. Inflation
26.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
26.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

27. Customer support
27.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
27.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

28. Change of address
28.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
28.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

29. Notices
29.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
29.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.2  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.3  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.4  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.5  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Freezer contents
III.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
III.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART IV: Reasonable precautions
IV.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
IV.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART V: Changes in circumstances
V.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
V.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART VI: Taxes
VI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
VI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART VII: Payment of claims
VII.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
VII.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART VIII: Fraud
VIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
VIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART IX: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
IX.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
IX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
IX.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
IX.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
IX.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART X: Flood
X.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
X.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
X.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
X.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XI: Cooperation
XI.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
XI.2  The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART XII: Currency
XII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XIII: Customer support
XIII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XIII.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART XIV: General exclusions
XIV.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
XIV.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART XV: Duty of fair presentation
XV.1  The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
XV.2  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XV.3  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XVI: Cancellation
XVI.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XVI.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XVI.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XVII: Compensation scheme
XVII.1  The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XVII.2  If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XVIII: Salvage
XVIII.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XVIII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XIX: Exchange of information
XIX.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
XIX.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

PART XX: Assignment
XX.1  The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

PART XXI: Environmental commitment
XXI.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXI.2  The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXII: Recovery of costs
XXII.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XXIII: Claims documents
XXIII.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIV: Making a claim
XXIV.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XXIV.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXIV.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART XXV: Instalment agreements
XXV.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXV.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXVI: Inflation
XXVI.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXVI.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXVII: Sanctions
XXVII.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXVIII: Data protection
XXVIII.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXVIII.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXVIII.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.

I.7  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.8  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.
I.20  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

1.12 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.13 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

1.16 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

1.18 Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.19 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
3.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
3.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
3.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 4 - THERAPY SERVICES
4.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
4.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
4.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
4.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 5 - DENTAL CARE
5.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
5.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
5.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
5.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
5.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
5.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 6 - VISION CARE
6.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
6.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
6.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
6.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.4 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.5 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
9.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
9.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 10 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
10.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
10.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 11 - CANCELLATION
11.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
11.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
11.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 12 - DISCOUNTS
12.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
12.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 13 - FRAUD
13.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
13.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 14 - INTERPRETATION
14.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
14.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
14.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 15 - COOPERATION
15.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
15.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 16 - SALVAGE
16.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
16.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 17 - GOVERNING LAW
17.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
17.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 18 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
18.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
18.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 19 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
19.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
19.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 20 - DATA PROTECTION
20.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
20.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
20.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 21 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
21.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
21.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 22 - CURRENCY
22.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
22.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 23 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
23.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
23.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
23.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 24 - TAXES
24.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
24.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 25 - RENEWAL
25.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
25.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 26 - DEPENDANTS
26.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
26.2 Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

SECTION 27 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
27.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
27.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 28 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
28.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
28.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 29 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
29.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
29.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 30 - COMMUNICATION
30.1 We will communicate with you in English.
30.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 31 - APPEALS
31.1 If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
31.2 An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
31.3 We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

SECTION 32 - SUBROGATION
32.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
32.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 33 - SEVERABILITY
33.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 34 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
34.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
34.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 35 - ASSIGNMENT
35.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 36 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
36.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
36.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 37 - INTEREST
37.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 38 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
38.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
38.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 39 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
39.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 40 - ELIGIBILITY
40.1 Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
40.2 Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

SECTION 41 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
41.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
41.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 42 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
42.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
42.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
42.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 43 - OTHER INSURANCE
43.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
43.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 44 - WELLNESS ALLOWANCE
44.1 Each plan year you may claim up to $150 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
44.2 The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SECTION 45 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
45.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
45.2 If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.
