# Gadget Cover: Terms and Conditions
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.4** Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
- **1.5** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.6** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.7** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.10** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.11** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.12** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.15** Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
- **1.16** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Interest
- **3.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 4. Unrecoverable devices
- **4.1** If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
- **4.2** We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

## 5. Duty of fair presentation
- **5.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **5.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **5.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 6. Third-party administrators
- **6.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **6.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 7. Customer support
- **7.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **7.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 8. Breakdown
- **8.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **8.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **8.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
- **8.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **8.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 9. Electronic documents
- **9.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **9.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **9.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 10. Reasonable precautions
- **10.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **10.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 11. Automatic renewal
- **11.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **11.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 12. Cooperation
- **12.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **12.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 13. Fraud
- **13.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **13.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 14. Communication
- **14.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **14.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 15. Other insurance
- **15.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **15.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 16. Waiver
- **16.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 17. Transferring the plan
- **17.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **17.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 18. Data protection
- **18.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **18.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **18.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 19. Interpretation
- **19.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **19.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **19.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 20. Governing law
- **20.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **20.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 21. Claims documents
- **21.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **21.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 22. Inflation
- **22.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **22.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 23. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **23.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **23.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **23.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **23.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **23.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 24. Changes in circumstances
- **24.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **24.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 25. Accidental Damage
- **25.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **25.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **25.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **25.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **25.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 26. Assignment
- **26.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 27. Subrogation
- **27.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **27.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 28. General exclusions
- **28.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **28.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **28.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **28.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

## 29. Discounts
- **29.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **29.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 30. Instalment agreements
- **30.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **30.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 31. Market conditions
- **31.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 32. Exchange of information
- **32.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **32.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 33. Premium payment
- **33.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **33.2** If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 34. Making a claim
- **34.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **34.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **34.3** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 35. Complaints
- **35.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **35.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **35.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 36. Replacement devices
- **36.1** If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
- **36.2** Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
- **36.3** Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

## 37. Currency
- **37.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **37.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 38. Renewal
- **38.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **38.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 39. Change of address
- **39.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **39.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 40. Recovery of costs
- **40.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 41. How to read this document
- **41.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **41.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **41.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 42. Repair process
- **42.1** After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
- **42.2** We aim to return repaired devices within 5 business days of receiving them.

## 43. Salvage
- **43.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **43.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 44. Notices
- **44.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **44.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 45. Severability
- **45.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 46. Joint policyholders
- **46.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **46.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 47. Geographical limits
- **47.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **47.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 48. Sanctions
- **48.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 49. Arbitration
- **49.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **49.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 50. Cancellation
- **50.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **50.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
- **50.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 51. Compensation scheme
- **51.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **51.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 52. Records and evidence
- **52.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **52.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **52.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 53. Payment of claims
- **53.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **53.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 54. Data and backups
- **54.1** We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
- **54.2** You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

## 55. Taxes
- **55.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **55.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 56. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **56.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 57. Software support
- **57.1** Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
- **57.2** Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

## 58. Environmental commitment
- **58.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **58.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 59. Accessibility
- **59.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Circuit Care Services

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2 Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.4 Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.5 Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
1.6 Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.7 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.8 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.9 Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
1.10 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.11 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.12 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.13 Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.14 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.15 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.16 Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND SERVICE FEE
2.1 Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
2.2 Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.3 Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.4 The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
3.1 We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
3.2 The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
3.5 We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

SECTION 4 - OPTIONAL COVER: THEFT AND LOSS
4.1 We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
4.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3 The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5 We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

SECTION 5 - BREAKDOWN
5.1 We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
5.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
5.3 The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
5.5 We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

SECTION 6 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
6.1 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
6.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.3 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
6.4 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
6.5 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
6.6 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 7 - MAKING A CLAIM
7.1 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
7.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
7.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 8 - SUBROGATION
8.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
8.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 9 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
9.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
9.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
9.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 10 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
10.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
10.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
10.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 11 - TRANSFERRING THE PLAN
11.1 You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
11.2 The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

SECTION 12 - GOVERNING LAW
12.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
12.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 13 - INFLATION
13.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
13.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 14 - COMMUNICATION
14.1 We will communicate with you in English.
14.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 15 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
15.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
15.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 16 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
16.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
16.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 17 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
17.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
17.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 18 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
18.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
18.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 19 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
19.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
19.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 20 - TAXES
20.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
20.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 21 - SOFTWARE SUPPORT
21.1 Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
21.2 Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

SECTION 22 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
22.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
22.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 23 - DATA AND BACKUPS
23.1 We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
23.2 You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

SECTION 24 - RENEWAL
24.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
24.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 25 - ARBITRATION
25.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
25.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 26 - SANCTIONS
26.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 27 - INTEREST
27.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 28 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
28.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
28.2 If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 29 - REPAIR PROCESS
29.1 After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
29.2 We aim to return repaired devices within 15 business days of receiving them.

SECTION 30 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
30.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 31 - REPLACEMENT DEVICES
31.1 If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
31.2 Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
31.3 Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

SECTION 32 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
32.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
32.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 33 - UNRECOVERABLE DEVICES
33.1 If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
33.2 We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

SECTION 34 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
34.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
34.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 35 - ASSIGNMENT
35.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 36 - DISCOUNTS
36.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
36.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 37 - SALVAGE
37.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
37.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 38 - COMPLAINTS
38.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
38.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
38.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 39 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
39.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 40 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
40.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
40.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 41 - DATA PROTECTION
41.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
41.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
41.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 42 - OTHER INSURANCE
42.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
42.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 43 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
43.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
43.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 44 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
44.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
44.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 45 - COOPERATION
45.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
45.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 46 - MARKET CONDITIONS
46.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 47 - FRAUD
47.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
47.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 48 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
48.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
48.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 49 - INTERPRETATION
49.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
49.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
49.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 50 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
50.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
50.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
50.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 51 - SEVERABILITY
51.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 52 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
52.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
52.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 53 - ACCESSIBILITY
53.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 54 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
54.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
54.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 55 - NOTICES
55.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
55.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 56 - CANCELLATION
56.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
56.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
56.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 57 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
57.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
57.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
57.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 58 - CURRENCY
58.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
58.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 59 - WAIVER
59.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(b) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 4. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 5. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 6. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 7. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 8. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 9. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 10. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 11. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 12. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 13. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 14. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 15. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 16. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 17. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 18. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 19. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 20. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 21. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 22. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 23. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 24. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 25. Third-party administrators

(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 1

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.3. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.4. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.5. Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.6. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.8. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.9. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.10. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.11. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.12. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.15. Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Inflation
3.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
3.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

4. Change of address
4.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
4.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

5. Fraud
5.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
5.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

6. Renewal
6.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
6.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

7. Recovery of costs
7.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

8. Interest
8.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

9. Eligibility
9.1. Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
9.2. Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

10. Therapy Services
10.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
10.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
10.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
10.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

11. Premium payment
11.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
11.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

12. Discounts
12.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
12.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

13. Salvage
13.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
13.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

14. Governing law
14.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
14.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

15. Optional cover: Hearing Care
15.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
15.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
15.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
15.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

16. Assignment
16.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

17. Severability
17.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

18. Subrogation
18.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
18.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

19. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
19.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

20. Vision Care
20.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
20.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
20.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
20.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

21. Dependants
21.1. You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
21.2. Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

22. Changes in circumstances
22.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
22.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

23. Environmental commitment
23.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
23.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

24. Reasonable precautions
24.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
24.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

25. Other insurance
25.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
25.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

26. Sanctions
26.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

27. Currency
27.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
27.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

28. Leaving the plan
28.1. Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
28.2. Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

29. Arbitration
29.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
29.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

30. Notices
30.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
30.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

31. Waiver
31.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

32. Appeals
32.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
32.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
32.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

33. Dental Care
33.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
33.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
33.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
33.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
33.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
33.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

34. How to read this document
34.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
34.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
34.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

35. Coordination of benefits
35.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
35.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

36. General exclusions
36.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
36.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
36.3. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
36.4. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
36.5. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

37. Cooperation
37.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
37.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

38. Compensation scheme
38.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
38.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

39. Geographical limits
39.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
39.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

40. Customer support
40.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
40.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

41. Payment of claims
41.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
41.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

42. Automatic renewal
42.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
42.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

43. Third-party administrators
43.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
43.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

44. Electronic documents
44.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
44.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
44.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

45. Making a claim
45.1. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
45.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
45.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

46. Joint policyholders
46.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
46.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

4.1 We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.

5.1 We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
5.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.

6.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

6.4 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

7.1 You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

7.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 8 - SALVAGE
8.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
8.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 9 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
9.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 10 - CANCELLATION
10.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
10.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
10.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 11 - COOPERATION
11.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.

SECTION 12 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT

13.1 Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.

14.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 15 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
15.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
15.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 16 - ASSIGNMENT
16.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 17 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
17.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
17.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
17.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 18 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
18.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 19 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
19.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
19.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 20 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
20.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
20.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
20.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 21 - RENEWAL
21.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
21.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 22 - TRANSFERRING THE PLAN
22.1 You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
22.2 The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

SECTION 23 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
23.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
23.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
23.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 24 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
24.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
24.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 25 - INTERPRETATION
25.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
25.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
25.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 26 - REPAIR PROCESS
26.1 After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
26.2 We aim to return repaired devices within 15 business days of receiving them.

SECTION 27 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
27.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
27.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 28 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
28.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
28.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 29 - ARBITRATION

SECTION 30 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 1

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3. Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.4. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.5. Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.6. Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.7. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.8. High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.9. Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.10. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.11. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.12. Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.15. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.19. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.20. Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Sanctions
3.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

4. How to read this document
4.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
4.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
4.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

5. Change of address

5.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

6. Geographical limits
6.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
6.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

7. Interest
7.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

8. Subrogation
8.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
8.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

9. Governing law
9.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
9.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

10. Communication

10.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

11. Alternative accommodation
11.1. If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
11.2. We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
11.3. Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

12. Assignment
12.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

13. Contents temporarily removed
13.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
13.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

14. Automatic renewal
14.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
14.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

15. Tenant's improvements
15.1. If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
15.2. This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

16. Electronic documents
16.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
16.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
16.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

17. Severability
17.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

18. Salvage
18.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
18.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

19. Waiver
19.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

20. Escape of Water
20.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
20.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
20.3. We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
20.4. We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

21. Instalment agreements
21.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
21.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

22.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
22.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

23.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
23.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

24.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
24.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

25.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

26.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.

27.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
27.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

28.1. We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
28.2. The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
28.3. The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
28.4. We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
28.5. We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
28.6. We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

29.1. We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
29.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
29.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
29.4. We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
29.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

30. Flood
30.1. We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
30.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
30.3. The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
30.4. We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

31. Discounts
31.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
31.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

32. Claims documents
32.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
32.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

33. Inflation
33.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
33.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

34. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
34.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

35. Premium payment
35.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
35.2. If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

36. Data protection
36.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
36.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
36.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

37. Complaints
37.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
37.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
37.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

38. Currency
38.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
38.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

39. Changes in circumstances
39.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
39.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

40. Payment of claims
40.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
40.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

41. Freezer contents
41.1. We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
41.2. We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

42. Other insurance
42.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
42.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

43. General exclusions
43.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
43.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
43.3. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
43.4. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
43.5. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

44. Joint policyholders
44.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
44.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

45. Locks and keys
45.1. If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
45.2. The most we will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

46. Making a claim
46.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
46.2. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
46.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

47. Duty of fair presentation
47.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
47.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
47.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

(d) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(e) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

Article 4. Breakdown
(a) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(e) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

Article 5. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(a) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(c) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
(d) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

Article 6. General exclusions
(a) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(d) The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.

Article 7. Making a claim
(a) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 8. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.

(b) Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 10. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 11. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 12. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Customer must tell the Provider as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Provider may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 13. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Customer pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

(a) When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

(a) If the Provider does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Provider has given up the right to enforce it later.

(a) Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 17. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 18. Change of address
(a) The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
(b) The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 19. Transferring the plan
(a) The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
(b) The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

Article 20. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 21. Data and backups
(a) The Provider is not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on the Customer's device.
(b) The Customer should back up the Customer's data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

Article 22. Data protection
(a) The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

Article 23. Premium payment
(a) The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 24. Assignment
(a) The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

Article 25. Cancellation
(a) The Customer can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Customer can cancel at any time; the Provider will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Provider can cancel this policy by giving the Customer 30 days' written notice to the last address the Provider holds.

Article 26. Inflation
(a) The Provider may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Customer's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 27. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
(b) If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Customer gives incorrect information carelessly, the Provider may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 28. Subrogation
(a) The Provider will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Customer's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Provider can take action in the Customer's name to recover any payment the Provider makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 29. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Provider may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 30. Replacement devices
(a) If the Provider cannot repair the Customer's device economically, the Provider will replace it with a replacement device.
(b) Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
(c) Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

Article 31. Complaints
(a) If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 32. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Customer must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Customer must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.
